items.reason: setup configures both ultrasonic sensors (Trig 8/Echo 9, Trig 10/Echo 11), red LED D12, green LED D13, buzzer D6, and TM1637 constructed with CLK=4/DIO=5 with brightness set.
When risk (overlap of both approaches within distance thresholds sustained 120ms), red LED toggles via now%1000<500, buzzer tone set to 1000Hz, and display shows level (1 or 2).
Green LED output is set to !risk, so it is HIGH (on) whenever no danger, and written to pin 13 each loop.
On falling edge of risk, serial trigger fires and duration (now-entered) is computed and printed to Serial.
setup configures A0/A1/A2 as inputs, attaches servo to D9, constructs TM1637 with CLK=4/DIO=5, sets D6 output and D2 input pullup.
In auto mode (autoManual false), balance=io_1-io_0 (A1-A0) drives angle to 45/135/90, and angle is written to servo D9.
io_2 (A2 voltage) is compared to threshold 614 to derive lowNow/low, and display alternates between charge-state indicator and scaled voltage.
Button io_6 edge toggles sysml_state_autoManual, and auto branch is gated on !sysml_state_autoManual, switching between auto and manual modes.
When low persists >=10000ms, alarm sets tone value 1000 (drives D6) and serial trigger prints "low charge" once.
DHT11 on pin 7 is initialized and read in loop; readTemperature result is stored into hw_value_io_3 and passed to ProgramPage1 as io_3.
A0 is configured as input and analogRead(A0) is sampled into hw_value_io_0, which is passed as io_0 and scaled to a threshold in ProgramPage1.
TM1637 constructed with CLK=4, DIO=5; io_5 alternates between threshold and current temperature every 2s and is shown via showNumberDec.
io_1 = valid && temp>threshold drives D13 HIGH (steady on); io_2 becomes 1000 when alarm active and now%1000<400, producing periodic tone on D6 via tone()/noTone().
After init, showTempMode is false, so io_8 is set to peopleCount (0), and loop displays it on the TM1637 via showNumberDec.
When entrance (io_1) is detected first, lastEntranceValid is set; a subsequent exit (io_3) increments peopleCount.
When exit (io_3) is detected without a prior entrance, lastEntranceValid is false, so peopleCount is decremented.
Button D2 edge toggles showTempMode; when true, io_8 becomes the truncated temperature, which loop displays on TM1637.
Fan PWM io_7 is set to 100 whenever peopleCount>0, independent of temperature; temperature is not used in the fan calculation.
When peopleCount is 0, io_7 is set to 0.0, and loop writes that to the fan PWM pin, turning it off.
Fan PWM uses pin 5 and TM1637 is constructed with DIO pin 3 (CLK 4), so D5 is not shared with TM1637 DIO; no pin conflict exists in the code.
Setup initializes A0/A1, D2, D5, D10, D6, TM1637 and Serial, but the TM1637 is constructed with CLK=4, DIO=3, while the authoritative wiring requires DIO=D5. The display is wired to the wrong pin.
Fan output io_3 is computed from ambient io_0: when door closed and not defrosting, io_0>2500 gives 255 else 128, and 0 otherwise; loop writes it to D5 via analogWrite.
inDefrost is set true when evaporator io_1>=1000 and otherwise retains prior state; io_4 output drives D10 relay, so evaporator temperature determines defrost entry.
When door io_2 is open, doorOpenElapsedMs accumulates io_7 (elapsed ms); fan output is forced to 0 while door open, pausing fan control.
Ambient io_0>=3000 sets alarmLevel=1, which drives buzzer tone 1000 and serial detailed status output (alarm_level, temps, door).
Evaporator io_1>=2000 sets alarmLevel=1, producing buzzer tone and serial detailed status output.
Door open elapsed >=600000 ms sets alarmLevel=2, giving buzzer tone 2000 and serial detailed status output.
setup() configures all required pins: analog inputs A0/A1/A2, outputs 10/13/6, TM1637 constructed with CLK=4,DIO=5, and button pin 2 as INPUT_PULLUP.
In auto mode pump is true only when water present (io_2>=512), soil dry (io_0<512) and not raining (io_1>=512); output drives relay D10.
The pump expression ANDs water, dry-soil, and no-rain conditions, so failing any one yields pump=false and relay LOW.
When water insufficient (io_2<512), water=false forces pump false (relay off) and io_5=1000 drives buzzer tone on D6.
Button edge (io_7 rising) toggles automatic false when in auto mode, switching to manual.
In manual mode a button press sets forced=true with began=millis(), and forced clears after 5000ms; pump is true while forced.
Display page cycles every 2s through 3 phases showing soil (io_0), water (io_2), and mode (0 auto/1 manual), written to TM1637.

setup initializes pins, buzzer, LED, and display, but the display shows hw_value_io_6 which is only set by ProgramPage1 in loop; at startup it is 0 and no load percentage is ever computed or displayed. The load percentage is never derived from A0 (io_3 is unused in ProgramPage1), so the required floor+load display is not implemented.

The over-limit check uses sysml_state_loadPercent, which is never assigned from the A0 reading (io_3 is unused), so it stays 0 and the buzzer never activates. Also the button branch sets pendingMove/targetFloor before any load check, so floor changes are not prevented on over-limit.

Button press edge sets targetFloor (1/2/3) and a 1000ms moveRemainingMs; when it reaches <=0 currentFloor becomes targetFloor and movementCompletePulse triggers Serial output. However moveRemainingMs is never decremented, so the delay never elapses and movement complete never fires.
The display only ever receives currentFloor (io_6 = sysml_value_2 = currentFloor); load percentage is never computed from A0 nor shown, so the required floor+load display is absent.
setup() configures A0/A1 as inputs, D2/D3 as pullup inputs, D10 output, attaches servo on D9, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4/DIO=5, then loop runs.
In auto mode when light value io_0 > 400 (strong light), curAnglePercent set to 0 (closed) and light off.
When io_0 <= 400 (weak light), curAnglePercent=100 (open) and lightMode=true driving LED D10 high.
Temperature check (io_1 >= 30) is evaluated first and closes curtain (0) with light off, before the light branch, giving priority.
Button D2 edge toggles autoMode between true/false with debounce via prevBtn2.
In manual mode, button D3 edge increments manualAnglePercent by 10 (wrapping at 100), and curAnglePercent follows manualAnglePercent.
TM1637 displays curAnglePercent (clamped 0-100) via showNumberDec, satisfying the percentage display option.
串口解析只接受固定字符串 T1..T32 映射为整数，ProgramPage1 仅将 io_8 值 0/1/2 映射为硬编码的 startMin/endMin（如 10/20、30/60），无法接收并保存用户输入的任意开始和结束时间。
没有任何基于当前时间与 startMin 比较的“开始前 1 分钟”判断；绿色 D12 由 io_6 驱动，而 io_6 仅在 !occupied && !overtimeActive 时为真，与预约开始前 1 分钟无关，且无闪烁逻辑。
PIR/门磁触发时 occupied 置真并点亮 D13，但 TM1637 显示的是 io_3 数值（occupied 时为 1），并非字符串 "occupied"；显示路径只调用 showNumberDec。
overtimeActive 的条件为 startMin>=endMin（在 endMin>startMin 之后），实际几乎不可达；且串口只输出 start_min/end_min，从未输出 "overtime use"，蜂鸣由 io_2=1000 驱动但触发条件错误。
D7 以 INPUT_PULLUP 读取，按下（HIGH）且前一状态未按下时清除 occupied 与 overtimeActive，实现人工释放。
Init sets stage to 1 and setup calls ProgramPage1_Init, so the system starts in stage 1 (preheat).

Only D2 (io_1) is read and used to start running; D3 and D4 are sampled but never passed into any logic, and no code sets target temperature or duration from buttons. Durations are hardcoded 30000 and targets hardcoded.
When measured temperature io_0 >= target, beepActive is set true, producing tone frequency 1000 on pin 6 via tone(6,...).
When remainingMs <= 0, stage advances 1->2->3 and target/remaining are reset, implementing automatic stage switching at duration end.
Display shows only stage number (io_6 = stage); remaining time is never output to the display, and remainingMs is never decremented so it stays 0.
Serial logs only stage_id, measured temperature, and a constant 0 elapsed_delta; no stage transitions, target temps, or full flow events are logged.
Display page alternates every 2000ms via now/2000%2, showing temp when page 0 and distance when page 1; values are written to TM1637 each change.
hot = valid && temp>32; buzzer toggles on 400ms/1000ms cycle via now%1000<400, and serial prints ALARM_TEMP when hot.
near = valid && dist<15; same intermittent buzzer condition and serial prints ALARM_DISTANCE when near.
setup() initializes Serial, pins 2/3/A0 as inputs, 6 and 13 as outputs, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5.
When selection is 0 (default) and analog light value <300, night is true and armed becomes true, entering night arming automatically.
alarm requires armed && io_0 (PIR) && io_1 (door); on rising edge count increments, alarm drives buzzer/LED, and count is output to display.
ARM command parses to 1, sets selection=1, making armed true.
DISARM parses to 2, sets selection=2, so night is false and armed is false (disarmed).
STATUS parses to 4 and prints mode and event count over Serial.
RESET parses to 3, resets count to 0 and selection to 0 (clearing event count and mode state).
setup() initializes the model, Serial, A1/D2/D3 inputs, TM1637 on pins 4/5, buzzer D6, and LED D13, then loop() runs the monitoring update.
On rising temperature above 8, it prints a labeled event with GPS position, and warm drives io_4=1000 (tone on D6) and io_5 true (LED D13).
Rising door-open edge prints a labeled event with GPS position, and io_2 drives buzzer and LED outputs.
Rising shock edge increments the events counter (bounded at 9999), which is the recorded vibration/event count.
Display value alternates every 2 seconds between the event count and the current temperature.
GPS: lat,lon serial input is parsed into manualLatitude/Longitude and printed in event logs when valid.

When not locked (playerId==0) and reset not held, the loop scans buttons and on a new press sets playerId=i+1 then breaks, so only the first press is recorded; subsequent presses are ignored because playerId!=0 blocks the scan.
playerId is output via io_7 and the loop writes it to the TM1637 display when it changes.
On a recorded press beeping is set true, io_6 becomes 1000 for 200ms, and the loop drives tone(6,...) then noTone after the window.
After a press playerId!=0, so the button scan branch is skipped until reset sets playerId=0, locking other inputs.
On a recorded press serial trigger is set and winTime/playerId are output; loop prints timestamp and player id.
When D9 (io_4) is pressed, playerId is reset to 0, re-enabling the button scan branch.
Holding D9 for >=3000ms clears the wins array (cumulative stats) once.
setup() initializes Serial, A1 input, D2 input, D10 output, D6 output, TM1637 on pins 4/5, and D13 output; loop reads A1 via analogRead.
Temperature computed from A1 ADC, hysteresis sets cooling flag, and loop drives D10 from that flag.
Door-open duration computed from millis; alarm true when >10000ms; io_3 drives tone on D6 and io_5 toggles D13 every 500ms.
critical requires door open and temperature>8; serial trigger fires on transition and then every 1000ms while critical, printing the message.
io_4 alternates every 2s between temperature and door-open seconds, and loop displays it on TM1637.

On a rising edge of D2/D3/D4 the selected item is set and displayPhase reset; the display output alternates between the item number (phase<1000) and the price, so both number and price are shown on the TM1637.
On confirm release (short press, not admin, not hold-handled) with stock>0, saleItem is set, stock decremented, beep frequency/remaining set, and loop prints dispense:itemX based on saleItem.
When selected item stock is 0, displayError is set true and a 1000Hz beep is triggered; display output becomes -1 (error code) and the display shows it.
While D7 held, holdDuration accumulates elapsed time; at >=2000ms adminMode toggles and holdHandled set, entering admin mode on long press.
Serial parser accepts RESTOCK1/2/3 with payload, encodes item*10000+amount; in admin mode the model adds payload to the corresponding stock variable.

setup() initializes the TM1637 (pins 4/5), configures buttons D2/D3/D7 as inputs, buzzer D6 and LED D13 as outputs, and calls ProgramPage1_Init; the state machine starts in setting mode (active=false) with default durations, allowing configuration of three stages.
When not active, a rising edge on io_1 (D2) increments duration[selected] by 1000ms, increasing the current stage's countdown time.
When not active, a rising edge on io_2 (D3) advances selected to the next stage modulo 3, switching to configure the next stage's duration.
A rising edge on io_3 (D7) while not active resets measurements, sets stage=0, and sets active=running=true, starting the countdown.
When active and io_3 (D7) is pressed, running toggles, pausing the countdown while active remains true.
On stage completion, pulses=stage+1 sets a distinct beep count per stage, and stage increments so the next stage runs automatically; the buzzer toggles at 1000Hz for pulses*300ms.
When the third stage completes, complete=true is set, and loop() drives D13 HIGH via hw_value_io_5, keeping the LED on.
On completion, report triggers Serial.println("process complete") and loop prints each stage's measured elapsed ms.
setup() initializes button D3 (INPUT_PULLUP), LED D13, buzzer D6, TM1637 on CLK=4/DIO=5, vibration D2, water A0, and starts Serial; loop() runs the monitor each cycle.
Initial stage is 1 (inlet); io_3=phase is written to the TM1637 via showNumberDec, so stage 1 is displayed.
When water present and vibration detected, phase transitions to 2 (wash) and phase is output to the display.
When water absent and vibration present, phase becomes 3 (spin) and is shown on the display.
When vibration stops for 2s in phase 3, phase becomes 4 (end) and is displayed.
In phase 4 without acknowledgment, alarm drives LED blink (io_1) and buzzer tone (io_2) at 500ms intervals until acknowledged.
A button press edge in phase 4 sets acknowledged=true, which makes alarm false, stopping LED and tone.
Fault condition (not phase 4, water present, no vibration for 8s) triggers serial output of "wash fault" once.
Lighting output io_5 is set to 255 only when ambient light is dark (io_2<350) and a PIR was detected within 3000ms; this drives D9 via analogWrite.
When ambient is not dark or no PIR detected, wasLit is false and io_5=0, so D9 gets 0.
Each PIR detection refreshes motion=now, and lighting stays on while now-motion<3000, so continued motion extends the on time.
Direction is inferred from which side triggered first; a trigger from the opposite side within 4s increments count, estimating crossings.
io_4 carries the count and is shown on the TM1637 display each time it changes.
total accumulates lit duration and is emitted over serial every 5s via the trigger.
床按钮按下时只设置 callActive、highestBedId、oldestWaitingBedId 并将 ageOfOldestMs 置 0，从未记录呼叫顺序，也从未累加等待时间；ageOfOldestMs 始终为 0，因此没有记录等待时间。
确认按钮仅在 callActive 为真时清除状态并置 serialPending，但随后第 162-164 行在 io_3 为低时立即将 serialPending 清零；且串口输出只打印 wait_time_ms 和 bed_id，没有处理日志。
数码管只显示 oldestWaitingBedId 一个数字，没有显示秒数；且 ageOfOldestMs 从未累加，始终为 0。
任务文本指定 TM1637 CLK=D4，但代码将 TM1637 构造为 (8,5)，即 CLK=D8、DIO=D5，与要求冲突。
setup() initializes the model, serial, the three sensor pins as inputs, TM1637 brightness, buzzer pin, and LED pin, then loop() runs the state machine and drives outputs.
The three sensor reads are summed into count, which is the occupied-layer count.
The count output io_3 is written to the TM1637 via showNumberDec whenever it changes.
When a layer is vacant beyond 60000 ms and not yet reported, io_8 is set and loop prints 'restock needed'.
When full, the buzzer is only pulsed for 250 ms and io_5 drives the LED; no state locks new records (recordsLocked is never set/used), so the 'lock new records' behavior is absent.
On QUERY (io_7==1) the trigger is set and loop prints each layer's occupied state.
RESET parses to 2, sets reset, and the loop resets each layer's vacant timer and reported flag.
setup() initializes the model, configures sensor inputs (A1/A0/A2/D2), actuator outputs (D10/D9/D5), buzzer D6, and TM1637 display, then loop() runs the control update each cycle.
Heater output io_4 is set true when water level io_2 >= 512 and temperature io_0 <= 600, and D10 is driven from that value each loop.
Lighting PWM io_5 is set to 1023 when level ok and light io_1 <= 512, else 0, and analogWrite drives D9 from it.
Aeration pump io_6 is true only when water level io_2 >= 512, and D5 is driven from that value.
When level io_2 < 512, heater and pump outputs are false (off) and buzzer frequency io_7 is set to 2000, driving tone on D6.
Button edge toggles display mode state, but the display value io_8 is always 0 in every branch, so the TM1637 never shows temperature, light, or level values.
setup() initializes serial, LED D13, buzzer D6, Trig D8 output, Echo D9 input, and calls ProgramPage1_Init which resets state to standby (approachActive=false).
When approachActive, flashPhaseMs accumulates and wraps at 200ms; LED output is high while flashPhaseMs<100, giving a fast 100ms on/100ms off blink.
beepSequenceMs cycles 0-500ms; tone is emitted during 0-100, 200-300, 400-500 windows, producing three short beeps.
welcomePulse is set true on the transition into approachActive and printed once via Serial.println("welcome").
While approachActive and no detection, inactivityMs accumulates and when >=5000 approachActive is cleared, returning to standby.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (resets alertLevel to 0 = normal), Serial.begin, pinMode for A1/A0/D2/D6/D13/D12, and TM1637Display constructed with CLK=4,DIO=5 with setBrightness. All required peripherals initialized and state enters normal level 0.
level computed as 2 if flame or (hot&&smoky), else 1 if hot||smoky, else 0. A single mild exceedance (hot or smoky alone) yields level 1 = attention.
level 2 when flame (io_2) true OR both hot and smoky (multiple indicators exceeded).
In alarm, io_3 set to 1000 during first 500ms of each second, else 0; loop applies tone(6,1000)/noTone(6) accordingly, producing intermittent beeping.
When alarm and trigger (on entry or every 1000ms), Serial.println("fire alert") is executed.
io_6 cycles every 2s among level, temperature, and smoke value; loop displays it via showNumberDec. Level number and key values are shown.
setup() initializes Serial, A0, A1, D2 (INPUT_PULLUP), D5 output, D6 output, D13 output, and TM1637 with CLK=4/DIO=3; loop() continuously samples and calls the model.
When vibration is false, temp<=60, and current<=7, conditional_5 resolves to 0, which is the normal state code output via io_6 and serial value.
When current exceeds 7.0 (and not vibration/overheat), conditional_7=1, producing overload state code 1.
When temperature exceeds 60, state code 2 is produced and fan PWM value is set to 255, driving D5 via analogWrite.
Vibration true yields state code 3 and faultEntry trigger; serial prints fault code and buzzer tone is driven on D6.
Vibration is checked first in the state priority chain, so when vibration is true the state is 3 regardless of overheat/overload, and fault code 3 is emitted.
displayCycleMs cycles 0-6000; <2000 shows current, <4000 shows temperature, else state code, and the value is written to TM1637.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets manualFrozen=false, so the system starts in auto mode; loop() then reads A0 and drives D9 PWM and the TM1637 display from the mapped value.
In auto mode the raw A0 value is truncated to an int and written to D9 via analogWrite and to the TM1637 display each loop iteration, so light changes update both PWM and display.
A rising edge on D2 (pressed and not previously pressed) toggles manualFrozen to true; while frozen, the PWM and display outputs use the stored frozen values instead of live light readings.
A second rising edge on D2 toggles manualFrozen back to false, after which the outputs again follow the live A0-derived value.

setup() initializes the model, TM1637 display (pins 4/5), red LED D13, green LED D10, buzzer D6, button D2, and both ultrasonic modules (trig/echo D8/D9 and D11/D12); loop() reads sensors and drives display/LEDs/buzzer, so distance and occupancy are shown from startup.
Green LED (D10) is driven by io_6, which is true when entry distance <30cm and the parking spot is not occupied (<=20cm), matching entry-approach guidance.

Buzzer frequency is graded by parking distance (2000Hz <5cm, 1800Hz <10cm, 1200Hz <15cm, 700Hz <=20cm) and red LED io_5 is set for parking distance <5cm or within 5-20cm, giving tiered buzzer/LED feedback.
When parking distance <5cm, io_7 is set to 2000Hz continuously (tone held until value changes), and red LED io_5 is true, providing sustained alarm.
Button D2 edge detection increments displayMode mod 3; display value selects entry distance (mode 0), parking distance (mode 1), or occupied count (mode 2), and is written to TM1637.

setup initializes the model, configures A1/A0 as inputs, D5 as PWM output, D2 as pull-up input, and constructs the TM1637 display on CLK=4/DIO=3; loop then runs the control update. The requirement text mentions DIO=D5 but the resolved wiring is D3, which the code matches.
Button state is read from D2 (LOW=pressed) and passed as io_3; the model toggles modeAuto on a rising edge using previousPressed, giving press-to-toggle behavior.
Temperature is computed from A1 raw counts scaled to 0-500 (LM35 10mV/C), then mapped to PWM 0 at <=20C, 255 at >=50C, linear between; in auto mode this autoSpeed drives D5 via analogWrite.
Potentiometer A0 raw value is scaled to 0-255 as manualLevel, and in manual mode this value is selected as the PWM output to D5.
In auto mode the display value is the truncated temperature (with floor correction), and loop writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec.
In manual mode the display value is manualLevel/10 truncated (a 0-25 level), written to the TM1637.
setup() configures Serial, D2 input, D10 output, D6 output, D13 output, D8 output, D9 input, and constructs TM1637 on D4/D5 with brightness set.
On rising edge of proximity with valid non-low level, open is set true and opened timestamp recorded; loop drives D10 HIGH while open, and open is cleared after 3000ms elapsed.
When level is low (invalid or percent<20), open is forced false so valve stays closed, and io_5/io_6 drive buzzer tone and LED alarm.
Display value alternates between uses and percent every 2 seconds rather than showing both remaining percent and today's use count simultaneously; requirement is to display both.
Serial input is parsed; on "STATUS" command the trigger is set and loop prints today_uses and remaining_percent values.
setup() initializes Serial, pins 2/3/7 as inputs, 13 and 6 as outputs, and constructs TM1637Display with CLK=4, DIO=5, matching the required devices.
On a rising edge of D2 (io_0 high and prevD2 false), totalCount is incremented and the no-product accumulator is reset.
Display mode 0 shows totalCount; mode 1 computes a rate from totalCount/600*100 (per-minute target of 600) and shows it; the display is updated each loop.
When noProductAccumMs reaches 30000 and not stopped, alarmActive is set; the alarm edge sets serialGate and captures total/stop counts, which are printed to serial as the stop event record.
On D3 press edge, stopActive is set true and stopCount incremented; stopActive forces alarmActive true, and the alarm edge records the event via serial.
alarmActive drives io_3 (LED D13) and io_4 (tone 2000 on D6); loop writes D13 and calls tone(6,...) when alarm active.
On D7 press edge, displayMode cycles 0->1->2->0; mode 0 shows total, mode 1 shows rate, mode 2 shows stopCount, matching target/actual/stop cycling.
D2 press edge toggles running from false to true, and elapsed accumulates dt while running, so counting starts.
Same edge toggle flips running from true to false, halting elapsed accumulation.
D3 edge sets elapsed to 0 and stops running, resetting the timer.
Elapsed ms divided by 1000 is output and shown on TM1637 via showNumberDec on D4/D5.
Crossing 60s sets beeping with beepStart; tone output 1000Hz drives buzzer for 1000ms then clears, while elapsed keeps accumulating.
Init sets counter to 0; setup calls Init then displays hw_value_io_3 (initialized 0) via showNumberDec since previous is INT32_MIN, so 0 is shown at startup.
On rising edge of D2 (io_0) and counter != 20, counter increments; loop then displays updated value via showNumberDec when changed.
On rising edge of D3 (io_1) and counter != 0, counter decrements; loop displays updated value.
At counter==20, pressing D2 keeps counter at 20 (no increment), and value_0 becomes 1000 which is passed to tone(6,...) producing buzzer alarm.
At counter==0, pressing D3 keeps counter at 0 (no decrement), and value_0 becomes 1000 driving tone on pin 6 for alarm.
automaticMode state toggled by mode button press event and used to branch between auto and manual control paths.
In auto mode fanCommand computed from savedTemperature (DHT11) with PWM mapping and written to pin 5 via analogWrite.
Auto mode sets lightCommand from io_2 (A0 light sensor) and writes to D9.
Auto mode sets pumpCommand from io_3 (A1 soil) and writes to D10 relay.
Select button press event in manual mode cycles selectedActuator 0->1->2->0.
Manual mode uses io_4 (A2 pot) to set fan PWM, light and pump based on selectedActuator.
displayPhase cycles 0-6000ms and value_7 selects temperature, light, or soil value; shown on TM1637.
On fault, io_11 set to 2000 (tone freq) and tone(6,...) drives buzzer D6.
On fault reportEvent triggers serial prints of fault info for each sensor.
setup() initializes TM1637 on pins 4/5, LED on 13, buzzer on 6, ultrasonic Trig=8 output and Echo=9 input; loop() performs periodic ultrasonic measurement and display update.
After ProgramPage1 computes the distance, loop() writes it to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when it changes.
ProgramPage1 sets io_3 true when lastValidDistanceCm < 30.0, and loop() drives pin 13 HIGH/LOW from that flag.
For distance <15 (and >=8) the model outputs 140, and the tone gating produces a 1000ms period with 100ms on-time, i.e. slow beep, driving tone on pin 6.
For distance <8 the model outputs 220 and the gating uses a 250ms period with 100ms on-time, i.e. rapid beep, driving tone on pin 6.
modeIsTemp initializes true in Init and the display value is derived from lastTempC when modeIsTemp is true, so the default display is temperature.
Button press is edge-detected via previousPressed and toggles modeIsTemp, which selects temperature vs humidity for the display value.
When lastTempC exceeds 30.0 the PWM value becomes nonzero (102+), and analogWrite drives pin 5; below/at 30 it is 0.
PWM value increases linearly with temperature above 30 ((temp-30)*20+102), so higher temperature yields higher fan speed.

Requirement text assigns TM1637 DIO to D5 conflicting with fan PWM D5, while resolved_devices gives DIO=D3; code uses D3 for display and D5 for PWM, so the conflict is a requirement ambiguity rather than a code defect.
setup initializes Serial, A0/A1 inputs, D2/D3 pullups, D12/D13 outputs, TM1637 (4,5), both DHTs on 7/8, and ProgramPage1_Init sets display indices to 0, entering polling state.
When not manual, page=now/2000%6 cycles room=page/3 and metric=page%3, and io_12 selects data[room][metric] (temp/humidity/light) for the current room, driving TM1637.
Rising edges on io_8 (D2) toggle room and io_9 (D3) advance metric, set manual=true and changed=now, pausing auto-poll for 8s.
serial_0_trigger fires every 5000ms and loop prints all six fields (both rooms' temp, humidity, light) via Serial.
living/bedroom computed as valid && temp>32 && light>700; io_10/io_11 drive D12/D13, and serial_1_trigger prints room-level alarm messages on rising edge.
setup() initializes the model, Serial, proximity pins 2/3, TM1637 (4,5), buzzer 6, LED 13, button 7, and ultrasonic trig/echo 8/9, then loop runs the counting state machine.
When io_0 (D2) is high, not latched, and not full, countReusable increments.
When io_1 (D3) is high, not latched, and not full, countOther increments.

However, io_2 is set true unconditionally in ProgramPage1, so led1 is driven HIGH in setup and loop, contradicting the requirement that all LEDs be off at power on.
The analog reading (0..1023) is scaled by 99/1023 and truncated to an int, producing 0..99.

The units digit is shifted first (value/1%10) and the tens digit second (value/10%10); with two cascaded 595s the first byte lands in sr2 (sevseg2) and the second in sr1 (sevseg1), so tens go to sevseg1 and units to sevseg2.

io_2 (led1) is hardcoded true regardless of value, so led1 is on for all values, not only 0..33; additionally led2/led3 conditions use >=34/>=67 which is consistent, but the 'only LED1' condition fails because led1 is always on.
led2 is set when value>=34 and led3 when value>=67, so for 34..66 led1 (always on) and led2 are on while led3 is off.
For value 67..99, io_2 true, io_3 true (>=34), io_4 true (>=67), so all three LEDs are driven HIGH.
loop re-reads A3 every 5ms and recomputes outputs, updating displays and LEDs continuously.
The requirement to hold each state at least 2 seconds conflicts with the continuous-update requirement; the code updates every 5ms with no hold, and the ambiguity prevents a definite judgment.
Init sets servo angles 0 and ledOn false; setup attaches servos and writes hw_value_io_0/1 (0) and LED LOW before any button read.
First press of btn1 sets pending=1, mode becomes 1, output io_0=90 and io_2 true (LED on).
First press of btn2 sets pending=2, mode becomes 2, output io_1=180 and io_2 false (LED off).
When mode is 1 and event 2 (or vice versa) mode becomes 3; outputs are 0/0 and LED toggles with 2000ms on/off via modulo 4000.
In mode 3, a subsequent btn1 or btn2 press sets pending and after 2s gate transitions mode to 1 or 2, leaving flashing state.
Mode 1 is held until a new pending event is accepted, which requires 2000ms elapsed since began; so state persists at least 2s.
Mode 2 likewise is held until pending accepted after 2000ms since began.

setup() calls hw_shift595_io_1 with hw_value_io_1 = -1, which is invalid so segments=0, but then bits is inverted (~0 = 0xFF) and shifted out, turning all segments on rather than off. The display is not off at power-on.
ProgramPage1 computes seconds=millis()/1000 and outputs (seconds*2)%10, so each real second the value advances by 2. The loop calls it every ~10ms, and the display value tracks 2*seconds.
After computing hw_value_io_1, loop compares to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_1 to shift out the new digit, updating the display when the value changes.
The output is (seconds*2)%10, so only the last digit is shown; e.g., 12 seconds -> 12%10=2. The digit table indexes that value.
loop runs continuously, recomputing from millis() each iteration and updating the display whenever the value changes, so the timer keeps incrementing and updating.
loop() reads A3/A4 every ~5ms and calls ProgramPage1 then writes all LED outputs each iteration, so states update continuously from pot values.
io_2 (pin 2 = led1) is computed from io_0 (pot1) scaled by 255/1023 and written via analogWrite.
io_3 (pin 3 = led2) is computed from io_1 (pot2) scaled by 255/1023 and written via analogWrite.
io_4 is true only when both io_0 and io_1 equal 1023, and pin 4 (led3) is driven HIGH/LOW from it.
rgb1 R (pin5) and G (pin6) come from io_0/io_1 scaled to 0-255; rgb2 R (pin8) and G (pin9) likewise from io_0/io_1.
When both pots are 1023, the blue component (io_7/io_10) is forced to 255 while R and G are already 255, giving white on both RGB LEDs.
Both RGB LEDs use identical formulas from io_0/io_1 (io_5-7 and io_8-10), updated each loop iteration, so they show the same gradient.
analogRead yields 0-1023 and each output is scaled by 255/1023 (or forced to 0/255 at extremes), producing 0-255 values for brightness and RGB components.

setup() writes initial hw_value_io_0=true to pin 2 (led1 on), hw_value_io_1=false to pin 6 (led2 off), hw_value_io_2=true to pin 3 (rgb R on) and hw_value_io_3=false to pin 4 (rgb G off), with pin 5 (B) false; rgb1 common cathode so R on = red.
ProgramPage1 sets io_0=red, io_1=!red, io_2=red, io_3=false, io_4=!red where red=millis()/2000%2==0, so during first 2s led1 on, led2 off, rgb R on (red).
After 2s red becomes false, so io_0=false (led1 off), io_1=true (led2 on), io_2=false, io_4=true (rgb B on = blue), lasting until 4s.
millis()/2000%2 alternates every 2 seconds indefinitely, and loop() continuously calls ProgramPage1 and writes outputs, so the two states repeat forever.
setup() writes pin 2 LOW from hw_value_io_0 which is statically initialized false, so led1 is off at startup.
io_0 = tick%2 where tick = millis()/2000, giving 2s on/2s off indefinitely; loop drives pin 2 from it.
colors array {1,2,4,3,6,5,7} indexed by tick%7 yields R,G,B,Y,C,M,W sequence repeating indefinitely.
Color index advances only when tick (millis()/2000) increments, so each color lasts 2 seconds.
io_4 = tick%100 starts at 0 and increments each 2s tick, giving 00,01,...
tick%100 wraps from 99 to 0 on the next 2s tick, resetting to 00 and continuing.

The first shiftOut sends the units digit (value/1) and the second sends the tens digit (value/10). With sr1 feeding sevseg1 and sr2 feeding sevseg2, sevseg1 gets units and sevseg2 gets tens, reversed from requirement.
hw_shift595_io_4 builds segment bit patterns from digit table and shiftOuts them to the shift registers on A0/A2 with latch A1.
All outputs derive from tick=millis()/2000, so LED, RGB, and display update every 2 seconds with millis-based timing.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which clears all state, and all output globals default false; setup writes LOW to every LED and bar graph pin before loop runs.
Button 0 (pin5) rising edge toggles bit0 via bits^=1<<0, and io_0=bits&1 drives LED1 on pin 2.

Requirement text is self-contradictory (says btn1 lights LED2 but btn2 toggles). Code toggles bit1 on btn2 rising edge and drives LED2, matching the btn2/middle-bit intent, but the literal text conflicts.

Requirement text is self-contradictory (says btn1 lights LED3 but btn3 toggles). Code toggles bit2 on btn3 rising edge and drives LED3, matching the btn3/highest-bit intent, but the literal text conflicts.
Segments are set by equality to bits value 1..7, mapping decimal value to the corresponding bar segment; segment_7 (bits==8) is unreachable but 0-7 range is covered.

manual_debounce_input only requires 150ms of stable raw level before reporting; a press held 150ms+ is accepted, but a press shorter than 150ms is also accepted once it has been stable for 150ms after release? Actually stable is set to raw after 150ms; a short press under 150ms never reaches stable=true, so it is ignored. However the debounce sets stable=raw after 150ms regardless, and on release stable=false immediately. A press shorter than 150ms: raw goes true, changed=now; before 150ms elapses raw returns false, changed resets, stable stays false — so short press ignored. This matches requirement.
Init sets digit=0 and prevBtn flags false; setup writes digit 0 to the shift register and drives LED pin 2 LOW (off) since hw_value_io_3 is false.
On btn1 rising edge (io_1 true and prevBtn1 false), if digit != 9 it sets digit = digit+1.
When digit==9 and btn1 edge occurs, conditional is set to 0, wrapping to 0.
On btn2 rising edge, if digit != 0 it sets digit = digit-1.
When digit==0 and btn2 edge occurs, conditional is set to 9, wrapping to 9.
Parity computed via modulo-2 check; even digit yields io_3 true, and loop drives pin 2 HIGH (LED on).
Odd digit makes parity false, so io_3 false and pin 2 driven LOW (LED off).
After ProgramPage1 updates digit and parity, loop immediately writes the shift register (on change) and LED pin each iteration.

Debounce is only a 5ms sampling interval; the edge detector uses prevBtn updated every loop iteration, so a single mechanical press with bounce longer than 5ms produces multiple rising edges and multiple increments/decrements. No stable-state debounce delay is implemented.
setup initializes Serial, pins 2/3 as inputs, 13 as output, 6 as output, TM1637 on pins 4/5, and loop drives the display with the count value; count starts at 0 and is shown via showNumberDec.
D2 read as active-low; on rising edge of pressed state sets lightOn true, which drives D13 HIGH.
D3 read as active-low; on press edge sets lightOn false, driving D13 LOW.
LIGHT_ON parses to 6, which sets lightOn true and increments count; D13 driven HIGH.
LIGHT_OFF parses to 5, sets lightOn false, D13 driven LOW.
BEEP parses to 1, sets beeping with timestamp; output io_3 becomes 1000 for 200ms, driving tone(6,1000).
COUNT_RESET parses to 3, sets count to 0; display updates when value differs from previous.
Each local button press and each LIGHT_ON/LIGHT_OFF/BEEP command increments count; count is output to display via showNumberDec.
setup() initializes Serial, TM1637 on pins 4/5, button pin 2 as INPUT_PULLUP, and DHT on pin 7; loop() polls serial, button, and DHT, entering the command/input state.

TEMP parses to mode 3, but the humidity selection only treats mode 2 as humidity and mode 1 as alternating; mode 3 falls through to temperature only by accident of the ternary, but the display value is cast to int and shown, and more importantly the mode mapping is inconsistent with the intended TEMP/HUMI/BOTH semantics (TEMP=3, HUMI=2, BOTH=1). The display does show temperature for mode 3 via the ternary, but the mode numbering contradicts the requirement's command mapping and the BOTH default.
HUMI parses to mode 2; humidity flag is true for mode 2, so io_4 becomes the humidity value and is shown on the display.
BOTH parses to mode 1; humidity flag alternates every 2000ms based on elapsed time, toggling between temperature and humidity on the display.
Button on D2 is debounced; on rising edge (press) serialEnabled toggles, and serial output is gated by serialEnabled, so pressing toggles serial output on/off.
setup() initializes all outputs from hw_value_* globals which are zero/false, so all single-color LEDs (pins 2,3,4) and RGB channels (6-13,44) are driven LOW/0 at power-on before any mode logic runs.
Mode 2 branch computes per-channel values from rainbow bit patterns {3,6,5} (yellow, cyan, purple) with interpolation, and mode increments to 2 on button press after 2s.
Mode 3 sets all RGB channels to 192 (equal R,G,B warm white), and io_3 (led3 on pin 4) is true only when mode==3.
Mode 4 (mode==0 after wrap) leaves all RGB values at 0 and all three single-color outputs false, so all LEDs are off.
Mode 1 sets channel==led to 255 giving red/green/blue on rgb1/rgb2/rgb3 respectively, and io_1 (led1 on pin 2) is true only in mode 1.
Mode change is gated by (!started || (now-changed)>=2000), so presses within 2s of the last change do not advance the mode.
Mode 2 interpolates each channel linearly from current rainbow color to next over 1000ms using (time%1000)/1000.0, producing smooth transitions.
Single-color LEDs are driven from mode-derived booleans: led1 on in mode 1, led3 on in mode 3, all off in modes 2 and 4, matching the described indications.
Init sets modeManual=true and hw_value_io_0 starts at 0; setup writes 0 to pin 2 before any loop update, so LED is off and Manual Mode is initial.
In Manual Mode, io_3 (A3/pot1) is scaled by 255/1023 with clamping at 0 and 1023, and the result is written to pin 2 via analogWrite.
The Manual branch only uses io_3; io_4 and io_5 (pot2/pot3) are only referenced in the Auto branch, so they are ignored in Manual Mode.
When modeManual and stableBtn1Pressed rising edge, modeManual is set false (Auto Mode).
Auto branch uses io_4 (pot2) as minimum and io_5 (pot3) as maximum, interpolating between their scaled values; endpoints clamp to 0/255.
transitionElapsed accumulates elapsed ms and toggles at 2000ms; interpolation factor is transitionElapsed/2000, giving a 2-second smooth ramp between min and max.
When not in Manual Mode and stableBtn2Pressed rising edge, modeManual is set true (Manual Mode).
Both buttons use a 150ms debounce counter decremented by elapsed ms, and stable state is latched when the counter expires.
Mode switches occur immediately on button edge with no 2-second minimum dwell guard; the 2000ms value is only used for the Auto brightness transition, not for state persistence.

setup() writes initial hw_value_io_0=false (led1 off, good) but writes io_1/io_4/io_7=true, io_2/io_5/io_8=false, io_3/io_6/io_9=false, so RGBs show Red at startup. However loop() runs immediately and ProgramPage1 sets outputs from millis()/2000; at startup tick=0 gives color=1 (Red) and io_0=tick%2=0, so led1 off and RGB Red. Actually startup state matches. But the initial static values are overwritten by loop within 10ms. Startup behavior: led1 off, RGB Red — matches.
io_0 = tick%2 where tick=millis()/2000, giving 2s on / 2s off continuously.
colors[0]=1 -> color&1=1 (R), color&2=0, color&4=0, applied to all three RGBs synchronously.
colors[1]=2 -> R=0, G=1, B=0 for all three RGBs.
colors[2]=4 -> R=0, G=0, B=1 for all three RGBs.
colors[3]=3 -> R=1, G=1, B=0 (Yellow) for all three RGBs.
colors[4]=6 -> R=0, G=1, B=1 (Cyan) for all three RGBs.
colors[5]=5 -> R=1, G=0, B=1 (Magenta) for all three RGBs.
colors[6]=7 -> R=1, G=1, B=1 (White) for all three RGBs.
tick=millis()/2000 changes every 2000ms, so each color is held 2 seconds.
tick%7 wraps from 6 back to 0, restarting at Red.
Both led1 (io_0=tick%2) and RGB (color=colors[tick%7]) are derived from the same tick in one update, so they run simultaneously and independently.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets count=0, then calls hw_shift595_io_0(0) since hw_value_io_0 (0) differs from INT32_MIN, displaying digit 0 on both displays.
On rising edge (io_1 true and previousPressed false), count is incremented by 37 unless it would exceed 99.

First shiftOut sends units digit (value/1%10) to sr1 (sevseg1), second sends tens digit (value/10%10) to sr2 (sevseg2). Note this places units on sevseg1 and tens on sevseg2, which is the reverse of the requirement.
When count+37 exceeds 99, conditional is set to 0, resetting the display to 00.
After ProgramPage1 updates count, loop compares to previous and calls hw_shift595_io_0 to shift out new digits immediately.
Init sets score=0 and phase=0; setup drives LEDs low and writes digit 0 via shift595 since hw_value_io_6 starts 0 and previous is INT32_MIN, so display shows 0.
Phase 0 counts down 3000ms with LEDs off (phase!=1) and score 0; readyReport is true on first update, printing Ready Go!.
On beginRound a pseudo-random selectedColor 0..2 is chosen and phase set to 1, which drives the corresponding LED output.
When selectedColor==0 and stop button newly pressed, score increments, successReport set, finishRound advances phase; serial prints Good Job! xN with incremented score.
Wrong button press (any newly pressed button not matching selectedColor) sets wrongReport, printing Come On!, and phase remains 1 so player can retry within remaining time.
When remainingMs reaches 0 in phase 1, timeoutReport and finishRound are set, printing Time's up! and advancing to next round.
selectedColor==1 with back button newly pressed increments score, sets successReport, and finishRound advances round.
Wrong button during yellow round sets wrongReport, printing Come On!, and phase stays 1 for retry.
Timeout in phase 1 sets timeoutReport and finishRound regardless of color, printing Time's up! and advancing.
selectedColor==2 with forward button newly pressed increments score, sets successReport, and finishRound advances round.
Wrong button during green round sets wrongReport, printing Come On!, and phase stays 1 for retry.
Timeout in phase 1 sets timeoutReport and finishRound, printing Time's up! and advancing to next round.
After finishRound (non-final), phase 2 with remainingMs=2000 counts down before beginRound, giving a 2-second interval between LED activations.
For rounds <3, if selected color already seen it advances to next color, and seen flags are set per selection, ensuring all three colors appear within 5 rounds.
After round 5 finishRound sets phase 3, remainingMs 0, endReport; LEDs off (phase!=1), display shows score, and serial prints Game Over! Your score is N.

evidence.text: if (hw_value_serial_1_trigger) { Serial.print("Game Over! Your score is "); Serial.println(hw_value_serial_1_value_0); }

items.reason: At reset, ProgramPage1_Init sets displayedNumber=0, but the servo outputs hw_value_io_4/5/6 remain 0 and are never written in setup because the servo write is guarded by command != previous (previous=-1, command=0, so 0 != -1 is true and write(0) occurs). However the tens digit 0 maps to servo angles 30/60/90 in ProgramPage1, so on the first loop iteration servos move to 30/60/90, not 0. Also LEDs: units digit 0 maps to led1 on, so led1 lights immediately, contradicting 'all LEDs off'. The init state does not produce the required power-on outputs.
loop accumulates elapsed ms into elapsedAccumMs and when >=2000 subtracts 2000 and increments displayedNumber by 1.
After increment, if displayedNumber > 99 it is reset to 0.
unitsDigit 0-2 sets io_0 true (led1) and other LED conditions false; loop writes pin 2 accordingly.
unitsDigit 3-5 sets io_1 true (led2) and others false; loop writes pin 3.
unitsDigit 6-9 sets io_2 true (led3) and others false; loop writes pin 4.
tensDigit <=2 yields servo values 30/60/90 written to servos on pins 5/6/7.
tensDigit 3-5 yields 60/90/120 for the three servos.
tensDigit 6-9 (else branch) yields 90/120/150 for the three servos.
After ProgramPage1 updates displayedNumber, loop calls hw_shift595_io_3 when value changed, which shifts out both digits; display updates same iteration.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets ledOn false, and writes hw_value_io_0 (initialized false) LOW to pin 2, so LED is off at startup.
ProgramPage1 computes phase=millis()%9000 and sets output true when phase<1000, driving pin 2 HIGH for the first 1 second of each cycle.
For phase in [1000,3000) the condition is false, so output is LOW for 2 seconds after the 1-second on period.
For phase in [3000,6000) the condition is true, driving the LED HIGH for 3 seconds after the 2-second off period.
For phase in [6000,9000) the condition is false, so the LED is off for 3 seconds after the 3-second on period.
The modulo 9000 wraps the phase each cycle and loop() continuously re-evaluates, repeating the sequence indefinitely.

setup() attaches the servo and writes hw_value_io_0, which is initialized to 0, so the servo does start at 0°. However, the first loop() call immediately computes step=millis()/2000%36 and writes a new angle; at power-on millis() is small so step=0 giving 0°, but the requirement is satisfied at init. Actually setup writes 0° correctly. Re-examining: setup writes command 0 to servo, so start at 0° is implemented.
ProgramPage1 computes step=millis()/2000%36 and angle=(step<=18?step:36-step)*10, producing 0,10,...,180 then back down, each held 2000ms. loop() calls it and writes the angle to the servo.
For step>18 the formula 36-step yields 170,160,...,0 in 10° decrements, each held 2000ms via the millis()/2000 division, and loop writes these to the servo.
setup() initializes the model and writes the zero-initialized hw_value_io_* globals (all 0) to every RGB pin, so all LEDs are off at power-on/reset.
In phase 0, io_0=255 (rgb1 R=red) but io_3=0, io_4=0, io_5=255 (rgb2 R=0,G=0,B=255=blue) and io_6=0, io_7=255, io_8=0 (rgb3 G=255=green). That matches the required first pattern, so this is P not F.
Accumulated elapsed ms triggers phase advance at >=2000, giving a 2-second first pattern.
In phase 1, io_0=0,io_1=255,io_2=0 (rgb1 green); io_3=255,io_4=0,io_5=0 (rgb2 red); io_6=0,io_7=0,io_8=255 (rgb3 blue). Matches second pattern.
Phase 1 also lasts until accumulatedMs reaches 2000, then advances to phase 2.
In phase 2 (else branch), io_0=0,io_1=0,io_2=255 (rgb1 blue); io_3=0,io_4=255,io_5=0 (rgb2 green); io_6=255,io_7=0,io_8=0 (rgb3 red). Matches third pattern.
Phase 2 also waits for accumulatedMs >= 2000 before transitioning, so third pattern lasts 2 seconds.
After phase 2, phaseIndex resets to 0, restarting the sequence indefinitely.
ProgramPage1_Init sets all three brightness globals to 0.0, and setup writes those zero values to pins 2/3/4 before any loop iteration, so LEDs start off.
On a rising edge of btn1 (io_3), led1Brightness is computed as pot1 (io_6, A3) times 255 divided by 1023, mapping 0-1023 to 0-255, and written to pin 2.
On a rising edge of btn2 (io_4), led2Brightness is computed from pot2 (io_7, A4) with the 255/1023 scaling and written to pin 3.
On a rising edge of btn3 (io_5), led3Brightness is computed from pot3 (io_8, A5) with the 255/1023 scaling and written to pin 4.

The stable window is set to stableTimer+200, but stableTimer increments once per loop iteration (~10ms), so 200 ticks is about 2 seconds only if the loop runs at 10ms; however the 'hold' branches merely self-assign brightness and do not prevent re-sampling, and more importantly the timer is a loop-count not a millis-based duration, so the 2s guarantee is not tied to real time. Also the hold condition only applies while the button is still pressed; once released, the brightness is not re-asserted but is also not changed, so it persists. The concrete defect: the 2-second stability is measured in loop iterations, not milliseconds, so it is not a real 2s guarantee.
When no button is pressed, none of the rising-edge branches fire and the hold branches only self-assign, so brightness globals retain their values and are re-written to the pins each loop.
Each button's rising-edge branch only modifies its own brightness variable and stableUntil; the other LEDs' brightness variables are untouched, so only the corresponding LED changes.
setup() initializes all output pins with the zero-initialized hw_value_* globals, so RGB channels write 0 and indicator LEDs write LOW before any loop iteration.
For io_0 <= 341, sysml_value_3 is true and the other two indicator flags are false, so only pin 2 (led1) is driven HIGH.
For 342..682, sysml_value_4 is true and the lower/upper flags are false, so only pin 3 (led2) is HIGH.
For io_0 >= 683, sysml_value_5 is true and the other indicator flags are false, so only pin 4 (led3) is HIGH.
In the lower third, sysml_value_0 is 255 and is written to pin 5 (rgb1 R) via analogWrite.
In the middle third, sysml_value_1 is 255 and is written to pin 6 (rgb1 G).
In the upper third, sysml_value_2 is 255 and is written to pin 7 (rgb1 B).
loop() re-reads A3 and recomputes outputs each cycle, writing all LED pins every iteration.

The requirement is ambiguous: the code only ever outputs 0 or 255 per channel (threshold-based), not a continuous 0-255 mapping of the potentiometer value; whether that satisfies the stated mapping cannot be determined.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init (resets state) then writes hw_value_io_0=99 to the shift registers and drives all LED/RGB pins LOW since hw_value_io_1..9 default false. Displays show 99, LEDs off.
ProgramPage1_Init sets countdownValue=9, and the display value is derived from millis()/2000 with digit=9-phase, so at step 0 digit=9.
digit=9-phase where phase=step%10 and step=millis()/2000, so the displayed value decrements by 1 every 2 seconds.
io_0=digit*11 produces repeated digits (e.g., 8->88) and hw_shift595_io_0 writes both digits to the two shift registers, updating on change.

The single-color LEDs are driven by color==0/1/2 which is the RGB phase, not a per-countdown-step sequence led1->led2->led3 each for 2s. The LED selection is tied to the RGB color cycle rather than a distinct LED sequence per step.
color cycles through 0,1,2 based on phase, and io_4/5/6 and io_7/8/9 drive the RGB channels accordingly, changing every 2 seconds.
When digit==0, io_0=0 shows 00, active is false so single LEDs off, and io_4..io_9 are all true (white) for both RGB LEDs.
phase=step%10 wraps, so after digit reaches 0 the next step restarts digit at 9, restarting the countdown.
In setup(), hw_value_io_3 is initialized to 0 (static double), and the guarded write block executes with command 0, calling write(0) on the attached servo before loop runs.
io_0 (A3/pot1) is scaled by 90/1023 into minimum, giving 0..90 degrees as required.
io_1 (A4/pot2) is scaled by 90/1023 and offset by 90, giving 90..180 degrees.
io_2 (A5/pot3) is mapped between minimum and maximum via minimum + io_2*(maximum-minimum)/1023, matching the required range.
loop() re-reads all three pots and calls ProgramPage1 then writes the servo each iteration (throttled to ~10ms), continuously updating position.
setup() initializes all hw_value_io_* to false and drives every output LOW before loop runs, so bar graph and both LEDs start off.
On a debounced stable press, currentCounter is pre-incremented by 1.
Bar graph outputs use currentCounter>N thresholds, lighting N segments for value N on pins 5-13 and 44 (A1-A10).
When increment exceeds 10, counter resets to 0 and overflowCounter increments modulo 4.
Overflow 0 yields both LED bits false, driving pins 2 and 3 LOW.
Overflow 1 sets bit0 true (led1 on) and bit1 false (led2 off), displaying 01.
Overflow 2 sets bit0 false and bit1 true, displaying 10.
Overflow 3 sets both bits true (11), and modulo 4 wraps next overflow to 0.
Raw input change resets timer; stable state only updates after 150ms of unchanged input, and only a stable press increments.
Counters are static globals only modified on a debounced press; outputs are recomputed each loop from persisted state, holding until next press.
Init sets both LED states false, and setup writes LOW to pins 2 and 3 before any loop iteration, so both LEDs start off.
On a debounced rising edge of btn1 (stable and not previously pressed), led1State is inverted and written to pin 2.
After a btn1 toggle, holdBtn1RemainingMs is set to 2000 and decremented by elapsed ms each step; further btn1 toggles are gated on holdBtn1RemainingMs being 0, keeping led1 stable for 2 seconds.
On a debounced rising edge of btn2, led2State is inverted and written to pin 3.
After a btn2 toggle, holdBtn2RemainingMs is set to 2000 and decremented each step; further btn2 toggles are gated on it being 0, keeping led2 stable for 2 seconds.
On a debounced rising edge of btn3, both LED states are set false regardless of prior state, and outputs are written accordingly.
After btn3 reset, holdBtn3RemainingMs is set to 2000 and while it is positive both LED states are forced false each step, keeping them off for 2 seconds.
Each button accumulates press time and only becomes stable after 20ms of continuous press, and toggles require a stable rising edge, providing debounce.
hw_value_io_0 is initialized false and setup writes pin 2 LOW before any loop update, so led1 is off at power-on/reset.
At reset colorIndex=0, but the RGB output values hw_value_io_1..6 are initialized to 0 and setup writes them before ProgramPage1 runs, so all channels are 0 (off), not red.
Servo1 and servo3 are initialized to 0 and 90 respectively, but servo2 hw_value_io_8 is initialized to 180 and written in setup, contradicting the required 0-degree init for servo2.
ledAccumMs accumulates elapsed ms and toggles ledOn every 2000ms, driving pin 2, giving a 2-second blink.
colorIndex increments every 2000ms and wraps at 7; the nested conditionals map indices 0-6 to red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, white on both RGB LEDs.
When servo1PosDeg==0 the servo update sets it to 180, and the value is written to servo1.
The else branch sets servo1PosDeg to 0 when it is not 0 (i.e., at 180).
When servo2PosDeg==180 the update sets it to 0.
The else branch sets servo2PosDeg to 180 when it is 0.
When servo3PosDeg==90 the update sets it to 135.
The else branch sets servo3PosDeg to 90 when it is 135.
Servo positions only change when servoAccumMs reaches 2000, giving a 2-second scan interval.
All three accumulators use the same elapsed time and 2000ms thresholds, so LED, RGB, and servo updates occur together and repeat continuously in loop.
Init sets digit=0; setup calls hw_shift595_io_2(0) which outputs digits[0]=0x3f (segments A-F) to the shift register, displaying '0'.
All bar graph segment outputs are initialized false and setup writes LOW to pins 4-13, so the bar graph is fully off at startup.
hw_value_io_0 and hw_value_io_1 are false at startup and setup writes LOW to pins 2 and 3, so both LEDs are off.
Accumulator adds elapsed ms; when >=2000 it subtracts 2000 and increments digit, wrapping 9 to 0.

The two shiftOut calls send units first then tens into a daisy chain (sr1 Q7S -> sr2 DS), so the last byte shifted ends up in sr1 (sevseg1) and the first in sr2 (sevseg2). Thus sevseg1 gets the tens and sevseg2 gets the units only if ordering is correct; here the first shiftOut (units) ends up in sr2 and second (tens) in sr1, which is actually correct ordering. However the inversion (~bits) makes segments active-low while the wiring expects active-high, so digits are wrong.

Loop continuously samples pots every 5ms, recomputes angles, and writes servo commands when changed, updating continuously.
Display value derived from servo1 angle each loop and shift register updated when value changes, reflecting pot1 in real time.

count increments by 1 per 2000ms step and each servo output is count*18, so each servo increases 18° per 2s up to 180.

All three servo outputs are assigned from the same count in one update, and loop writes all three each pass, so they update simultaneously every 2s.

The LED count is derived from the per-servo step count (0..10), not from the total of the three angles divided into 54-unit ranges; total=162 would be 3 LEDs but the code lights count LEDs where count is the per-servo step, not total/54.

Number of lit LEDs equals the per-servo step count, not total/54. At total=162 (count would be 3 per servo, total 162) it happens to light 3, but generally total=54 (count=1 per servo, total 54) lights 1 while total=108 (count=2, total 108) lights 2 — however total=162 with count=3 lights 3, but total=270 (count=5) lights 5 while 270/54=5, so it coincidentally matches only because all servos are equal; the requirement is total-based and the code is step-based, so it fails for the general mapping.
Segments are written to pins 5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,44 which match bargraph A1..A10 wiring.
setup() initializes pins 2/3/4 as OUTPUT and writes LOW because hw_value_io_0/1/2 are false-initialized, so the common-cathode RGB LED is off at power-on/reset.
phase = millis()/3000%4; for phase 0 (first 3s) io_0 true (red), io_1 false, io_2 false, driving pin2 HIGH only.
phase 1 sets io_0 true and io_1 true, io_2 false, driving red and green HIGH = yellow.
phase 2 sets all three outputs true, driving red, green, blue HIGH = white.
phase 3 sets io_0 false (phase<3 false), io_1 false, io_2 false, all pins LOW = off.
Modulo 4 on millis()/3000 wraps phase back to 0 after phase 3, restarting the sequence with red indefinitely.
pot1 (A3) read into io_0, mapped by io_0*180/1023, so 0 yields 0°, written to servo on pin 2.
1023*180/1023 = 180, within the 0..180 guard, written to servo1.
Linear proportional mapping from A3 reading to servo1 angle, updated each loop.
pot2 (A4) read into io_1; both io_3 and io_4 use io_1*180/1023, so 0 gives 0° for both servos.
1023*180/1023 = 180 for both servo2 and servo3, within guard.
Both servo2 and servo3 derive from same io_1 with identical formula, moving in unison proportionally.
Loop throttled to 5ms steps and only writes when command changes, giving smooth servo response.
All hw_value_io_3..12 are initialized false, and setup writes LOW to each LED pin before any loop update, so all LEDs are off at startup.

loop re-reads all three pots every 10ms and calls ProgramPage1 then writes all LED pins each iteration, continuously updating the bar graph.

In setup, hw_value_io_0 is 0 and hw_shift595_previous_io_0 is INT32_MIN, so hw_shift595_io_0(0) is called. For value 0, valid is true, so the first block (sevseg1) computes digits[0]=0x3f, inverts to 0xC0, and shifts it out — sevseg1 is NOT extinguished. The second block (sevseg2) uses valid && (value>=10L) which is false for 0, so segments=0, bits=0xFF, showing nothing rather than "0". Both required initial states are wrong.

The loop gates updates on hw_elapsed < 5UL, so it only recomputes every 5 ms, not every second. ProgramPage1 computes (millis()/1000*6)%100, which does increment by 6 per real second, but the display is refreshed far more often than once per second (every 5ms), and the value is recomputed from millis each time. The requirement is a per-second increment; the code updates continuously. Also the display only updates when the value changes, but the timing gate is 5ms not 1s.

ProgramPage1 takes modulo 100, so only the last two digits are retained. The display function only shows values 0-99 (valid = value<100), and the tens digit is shown only when value>=10. So values above 99 are reduced to last two digits.

102 % 100 = 2, so the value passed to the display is 2. For value 2, valid true, sevseg1 shows digits[2]=0x5b (the "2" pattern), and sevseg2 shows nothing (value<10). The requirement says displays show "2" — the units digit shows 2. This matches the last-two-digits rule.

The loop does continue running, but the update cadence is 5ms not 1 second, and the value is derived from millis()/1000*6 continuously rather than incrementing once per second. The per-second increment/update rule is not implemented as specified (updates every 5ms).

ProgramPage1_Init resets phase via static init and mode flags; loop calls ProgramPage1 which advances phase by elapsed ms mod 6000 and outputs red for phase<2000, green 2000-4000, blue >=4000, giving 2s per color from startup.
While not hold/off, phase advances and maps to red/green/blue each 2000ms window, cycling every 6s.
Rising edge on io_3 (k1) sets hold=true, freezing phase so current color is retained.
When hold is true phase stops updating, so outputs remain at the last color before the press.
Rising edge on io_4 (k2) clears hold and off, and phase resumes from its stored value, continuing from where stopped.
Rising edge on io_5 (k3) sets off=true, forcing all three outputs to 0.
With off true, all channel expressions evaluate to 0, turning the LED completely dark.
Loop runs every ~10ms, debounces inputs, and edge-detects presses each iteration, updating outputs immediately after state changes.

setup() initializes the shift register with hw_value_io_1=0, but the digit encoding inverts bits (~bits) and the 7-segment COM is tied to VCC (common anode), so writing 0x00 inverted to 0xFF lights all segments rather than showing "00". Also servos are only written if command differs from -1; with hw_value_io_3=0 the write is skipped, leaving servos uncommanded at power-on.
number is derived from millis()/2000%100, so it increments by 1 every 2 seconds; loop calls ProgramPage1 each iteration and updates outputs.
Modulo 100 wraps the number to 0 when it would exceed 99.
Each bar LED pin is driven by number/10 > k, so exactly the tens digit count of LEDs is lit.
servo1 (io_3) is set to units*18 and written to pin 12.

servo3 is set to units*18+120 only when units is nonzero; when units==0 it is set to 0 instead of 120, contradicting the formula.
No hold logic exists; sysml_state_holdServos and holdRemainingMs are declared and reset but never used, and servos are driven purely from the units digit each loop.
loop recomputes number and writes shift register, bar graph, and servos each iteration, so outputs update after each increment.
setup() initializes all hw_value_io_* to false and drives every output pin LOW before loop() runs, so all bar graph and RGB LEDs start off.
index cycles 0..7 and exactly one io_0..io_7 is true at a time, mapping to pins 8,9,10,11,12,13,44,45 = A1..A8, so one LED lights at a time in order.

For index 4-7, second=true drives io_9 (pin3=rgb1 G) and io_11/io_12 (pins5,6=rgb2 R,G) HIGH, giving rgb1 green and rgb2 yellow.

pot1 on A3 is read and passed as io_0; ProgramPage1 maps adc[i]*6.0/1023.0, i.e. 0..1023 to 0..6 sectors = 0..360 degrees, for i=0 (rgb1).

The sector/peak/ramp computation is a standard HSV-to-RGB conversion producing per-channel 0..255 outputs for each hue.
The conversion uses full-scale 255 for the peak channel and a ramp from 0..255, equivalent to S=1 and V=1 (maximum saturation and brightness).
Computed RGB values are written via analogWrite to pins 2-4 (rgb1) and 5-7 (rgb2), setting LED brightness.
loop() re-reads both pots and recomputes/writes outputs every ~5ms, so colors update continuously as pots change.
Hue is computed as a continuous position with fractional ramp interpolation across 6 sectors, giving smooth color transitions without abrupt jumps.
setup() calls hw_shift595_io_1 with hw_value_io_1 initialized to 0, and valid=0<100 so digits[0] (0x3f) is sent for both digits, displaying "00" at power-on.

First shiftOut sends units digit (value/1%10) to sr1 (sevseg1), second sends tens digit (value/10%10) to sr2 (sevseg2) via daisy chain.

Second press toggles ledState from false back to true, driving pin 3 HIGH (LED on).
Third press toggles ledState from true to false again, driving pin 3 LOW (LED off).
Fourth press toggles ledState from false to true, driving pin 3 HIGH (LED on).
Each new press (rising edge via previousPressed tracking) toggles ledState, so the alternating sequence continues indefinitely.
ledState is only modified inside the press-edge branch; with no press, previousPressed stays equal to io_1 and the output retains its value.
Init sets count=0; setup writes 0 to shift registers (digits 0x3f for both digits), drives all bargraph pins LOW (segments false), and servos write 0 since hw_value_io_2/3 are 0 and within range.

hw_shift595_io_0 shifts units digit (value/1%10) first then tens digit (value/10%10); with two cascaded 595s the first shifted ends in sr2 (sevseg2) and second in sr1 (sevseg1), giving tens on sevseg1 and units on sevseg2.

LED thresholds use count*10/99 rather than count/10, so e.g. count=50 yields 5.05 -> 5 LEDs (ok) but count=10 yields 1.01 -> 1 LED while requirement example implies proportional count/10; more importantly count=99 gives 10 LEDs and count=9 gives 0, so the mapping is percentage-of-99 not number/10. The example (50->5) happens to match but the proportional rule (number/10) is violated at boundaries like 9 (0 LEDs) and 19 (1 LED).

Servo angle is truncated to integer via (int32_t)(count*1.8) minus a fractional correction, so it is floored to whole degrees rather than the exact (number*1.8) value; e.g. count=1 gives 1 instead of 1.8.

Phase 0 sets io_0 (pin 2, rgb1 R) to 255 while G/B are 0, and segment_0 is true (phase>=0), lighting only A1.

Phase 4 sets white=true, driving all R/G/B channels of all three RGBs to 255, and all five segments true.
