Segments are cumulative from segment_0 (A1) upward, so lit segments always start at A1 and extend toward A5.
Modulo 5 on the phase index wraps phase 4 back to 0, restarting the sequence indefinitely.

setup() initializes servos from hw_value_io_9/10/11 which are 0, so servos go to 0°, but the RGB pins are written from hw_value_io_0..8 which are all false (LOW). With common-cathode LEDs, LOW on R/G/B means off, so LEDs are off. However, the first loop() call runs ProgramPage1 which sets phaseIndex 0 (red) and immediately drives the LEDs on and servos to red angles, so the initial off/0° state is not held; also servos at 0° only briefly. The initialization requirement is not satisfied because the first loop iteration immediately overrides it with red state.

phaseIndex 0..6 map to red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, white via the boolean channel logic: R on for phases 0,3,5,6; G on for 1,3,4,6; B on for 2,4,5,6. That yields red(0), green(1), blue(2), yellow(3), cyan(4), magenta(5), white(6) in order.
phaseTimeMs increments by 10 each loop and resets when (phaseTimeMs+10)>=2000, advancing phaseIndex, giving 2 seconds per color.
Phase 0 (red): servo1=0.0, servo2=45.0, servo3=90.0.
Phase 1 (green): servo1=45, servo2=90, servo3=135.
Phase 2 (blue): servo1=90, servo2=135, servo3=180.
Phase 3 (yellow): servo1=135, servo2=180, servo3=0.
Phase 4 (cyan): servo1=180, servo2=0, servo3=45.
Phase 5 (magenta): servo1=0, servo2=45, servo3=90.
Phase 6 (white): servo1=90, servo2=135, servo3=180.
When phaseIndex==6, next index wraps to 0, so the sequence repeats indefinitely.

setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which zeroes sysml_state_value, then writes the initial hw_value_io_1 (0) to the shift register via hw_shift595_io_1, producing digit 0 (0x3f inverted), and all bar graph segment pins are driven LOW since the segment booleans are false.
Accumulated elapsed ms is compared to 2000; when reached, value increments by 1 (unless 9, then 0). The loop passes elapsed time each iteration, so the display value advances every 2 seconds.
Each bar segment boolean is set true when sysml_state_value >= N, and loop drives pins 2..11 (A1..A10) HIGH accordingly, lighting N LEDs for value N.
When value equals 9, the next increment sets conditional to 0, and all segment booleans become false (value 0 < 1), so bar graph pins are driven LOW.

After ProgramPage1 updates value and segment booleans, loop immediately writes the shift register (on change) and all bar graph pins in the same iteration, so both outputs reflect the new number without delay.

Init sets servo state to 0.0; setup attaches servos and writes 0 (hw_value_io_2/3/4 are 0 and previous is -1 so write(0) occurs), and all segment globals are false so all bar pins are driven LOW at startup.
io_0 (analogRead A3 = pot1) is mapped to 0..180 with clamping at 0 and 1023, stored in servo1Deg and written to servo on pin 2.
io_1 (analogRead A4 = pot2) is mapped to 0..180 with clamping, stored in servo2Deg and written to servo on pin 3.
servo3 uses rounded average of io_0 and io_1 scaled by 180/1023 with 0 and 180 endpoints, written to servo on pin 4.
Each segment threshold compares rounded average scaled by 10/1023 against 1..10, so segment count grows 0..10 in order; segments map to pins 5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,44 (A1..A10).

Color index cycles through colors[] = {1,2,6,5,4,3,7} which maps to Red(1), Green(2), Cyan(6), Magenta(5), Blue(4), Yellow(3), White(7); all three RGB outputs io_0..io_8 are set to the same color bits, and pins 2-10 drive rgb1/rgb2/rgb3.
tick = millis()/2000, so color index advances once per 2 seconds.
digit = 9 - tick%10 counts 9..0, each value held for 2 seconds since tick increments every 2s; written to shift register via hw_shift595_io_9.
tick%10 wraps, so digit goes 9..0 then back to 9, repeating indefinitely.
For digit 7-9, (9-digit)/3 = 0, giving 0 degrees for all three servos.
For digit 4-6, (9-digit)/3 = 1, giving 60 degrees for all three servos.
For digit 1-3, (9-digit)/3 = 2, giving 120 degrees for all three servos.
digit==0 branch sets 180 degrees for all three servos.
Servo angle derives from digit which changes every 2 seconds (tick/2000), so each angle is held 2 seconds; writes only occur on change.
All outputs derive from the same tick = millis()/2000, so RGB, digit, and servo states all change together every 2 seconds.
tick is derived from millis() with modulo 7 and 10, so the sequence repeats indefinitely without termination.
setup() initializes RGB pins to hw_value_io_0..2 = true,false,false (Red) and writes io_6=0 to the shift registers, producing "00" on the displays.
colors array {1,2,4,3,6,5,7} maps to R,G,B,Y,C,M,W and colorIndex advances modulo 7, cycling the sequence.
Color index advances only when elapsed>=2000ms, so each color is held 2 seconds.
Both RGB LEDs are driven from the same color bits: io_0/io_3, io_1/io_4, io_2/io_5 are assigned identical values.
number starts at 0 and is written to io_6, displayed as two digits via tens/units digit lookup.
number increments by steps (elapsed/2000) each 2-second interval, so it advances by 1 every 2 seconds.
number is taken modulo 100, so after 99 it wraps to 00.
First shiftOut sends units digit (value/1%10) to sr1/sevseg1, second sends tens digit (value/10%10) to sr2/sevseg2.
hw_shift595_io_6 uses shiftOut on DS/SHCP and latches via STCP to push digit data to the shift registers.
Both color and number advance from the same elapsed/2000 step computation in one function, keeping their 2-second updates aligned.
Init zeroes intensities and runMs; setup writes zero PWM to RGB pins and LOW to all bar graph pins, so all outputs start off.
analogRead(A3) is scaled to 0-255 and stored into rgb[millis()/5000%3], so the pot adjusts whichever component is currently active.
rgb[] is static and only the active index is overwritten each step, so the other two components retain prior intensities and all three are written to the RGB pins.
count = io_0*10/1023 and each segment threshold count>n drives the corresponding bar graph pin, giving proportional segment count.
At 1023, count=10, so all thresholds count>0..count>9 are true and all ten segments are HIGH.
At 0, count=0, so every count>n comparison is false and all bar graph pins are LOW.
When millis()/5000%3==0, index 0 (red) is updated from the pot while rgb[1] and rgb[2] persist.
When millis()/5000%3==1, index 1 (green) is updated while red and blue persist.
When millis()/5000%3==2, index 2 (blue) is updated while red and green persist.
The active index is derived from millis()/5000%3, so each mode holds for a full 5000 ms window.
The modulo-3 index cycles 0,1,2,0,... indefinitely with 5000 ms per mode.
loop re-reads A3 every 5 ms and recomputes bar graph outputs each iteration, so the bar graph tracks real-time pot values.

setup() writes RGB outputs and servo positions using hw_value_io_* globals that are still zero; the potentiometer is never read and ProgramPage1 is never called before these writes, so initial color/positions do not reflect the initial pot value.
For io_0 <= 341, red is computed as io_0*255/341, giving 0 at 0 and 255 at 341.
For 342..682, green is (io_0-341)*255/341, giving ~0.75 at 342 and 255 at 682, increasing across the range.
For io_0 >= 683, blue is (io_0-682)*255/341, giving ~0.75 at 683 and 255 at 1023, increasing across the range.
rgb1 (pins 2-4) and rgb2 (pins 5-7) are driven from duplicated identical computations of the same io_0, so both LEDs get the same color.
Servo angle is computed as io_0*180/1023, mapping 0..1023 to 0..180 degrees, and written to each servo.
Each servo has an accumulator incremented by elapsed ms; the angle is only updated when the accumulator reaches 2000 ms, enforcing a 2-second hold.

Requirement is ambiguous: it demands immediate response while also requiring servos to hold 2 seconds; RGB updates each loop but servos only every 2s, so the intended interpretation cannot be resolved.
Globals hw_value_io_0..2 and io_5 start at 0; setup writes 0 to pins 2/3/4 (LED off) and shifts digit 0 to the display before loop runs.
io_3 (A3/pot1) is scaled by 255/1023 and assigned to both red (io_0) and green (io_1) outputs, which drive pins 2 and 3.
io_4 (A4/pot2) is scaled by 255/1023 and assigned to blue output io_2, driving pin 4.
Average of red+green+blue divided by 3 then 28.33, truncated to int with a correction for negative truncation, then displayed via digit table (0-9).
loop re-reads A3/A4 every 10ms, recomputes outputs, and writes analogWrite and shift register each iteration, updating continuously.
io_0 is read from A3 (pot1 SIG) and assigned to both red outputs io_3 (rgb1 R, pin 2) and io_6 (rgb2 R, pin 5).
io_1 is read from A4 (pot2 SIG) and assigned to both green outputs io_4 (rgb1 G, pin 3) and io_7 (rgb2 G, pin 6).
io_2 is read from A5 (pot3 SIG) and assigned to both blue outputs io_5 (rgb1 B, pin 4) and io_8 (rgb2 B, pin 7).
Each raw 0-1023 reading is scaled by 255/1023 to produce the 0-255 RGB value.

Requirement conflicts: task says sevseg1 shows red and green as two-digit numbers, detail rules say sevseg1 shows red mapped 0-9. Code packs red tens and blue ones into one value, matching neither unambiguously.

Requirement conflicts: task says sevseg2 shows blue as two-digit number, detail rules say sevseg2 shows blue mapped 0-9. Code drives both digits from a single packed value, not a clear blue-only display.
loop re-reads pots, recomputes values, and rewrites LEDs and shift registers each iteration (throttled to 5ms), so displays update continuously.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which zeroes displayValue, then hw_shift595_io_0(0) shifts digit 0 for both units and tens positions, so both displays show 0.

First shiftOut sends units digit (value/1%10) into sr1 (sevseg1), second sends tens digit (value/10%10) into sr2 (sevseg2). This is reversed from the requirement: sevseg1 should show tens, sevseg2 units.
All bar graph segment booleans are initialized false and setup writes LOW to pins 2-11; ProgramPage1 sets segment_0..9 based on count>N which is false at value 0.
analogRead(A3) is scaled to 0-99 via io_1*99/1023 and displayed each loop; digits computed from value. (Digit-to-display mapping is reversed per R002, but value determination and display occur.)
For value 0-9, count=value/10=0, so all segment_N = count>N are false, giving 0 LEDs lit.
For value 10-19, count=1, so segment_0 (count>0) is true and segment_1 (count>1) false, giving exactly 1 LED lit.
For value 90-99, count=9, so segment_0..8 (count>0..8) are true and segment_9 (count>9) false, giving 9 LEDs lit.
loop runs every 5ms, re-reads pot and updates displays and bar graph each iteration, so updates are continuous without noticeable delay.
At max value 99, count=9, so segment_0..8 are all true (count>0..8) and segment_9 false, lighting exactly 9 LEDs (indices 0-8).
loop continuously samples the pot every 5ms and updates outputs, with no blocking delays, keeping the system responsive.
Both servo value globals are initialized to 0 and setup() writes them to the attached servos, so both start at 0°.
All LED state globals default to false and setup() drives each pin LOW, so all bar graph LEDs are off initially.
Servo1 angle is computed as io_0*180/1023, giving 0 at 0 and 180 at 1023, a linear map.
Servo2 angle is 180 minus the same linear term, giving 180 at 0 and 0 at 1023.
Each LED threshold compares floor(io_0*10/1023) against 1..10, so the count goes from 0 at 0 to 10 at 1023 linearly.
At io_0=0, servo1=0, servo2=180, and all LED thresholds (>=1..>=10) are false, so all LEDs off.
At io_0≈512, servo1≈90, servo2≈90, and floor(512*10/1023)=5 so exactly 5 LEDs (thresholds 1-5) are lit.
At io_0=1023, servo1=180, servo2=0, and all ten thresholds are satisfied so all LEDs lit.
LEDs are assigned to pins 4..13 in order with increasing thresholds, so they light sequentially from A1 to A10 as the pot increases.
LEDs are driven only with digitalWrite HIGH/LOW from boolean states, so they are fully on or off with no PWM/partial brightness.
setup attaches servos and writes hw_value_io_0/1/2, which are initialized to 0, so all servos start at 0°.
RGB channel values and all bar segment booleans are initialized to 0/false, and setup writes those values to pins 2-4 and 8-45, so both are off initially.
io_0 (servo1) drives red via io_3, which is written to pin 2 (rgb1:R).
io_1 (servo2) drives green via io_4, written to pin 3 (rgb1:G).
io_2 (servo3) drives blue via io_5, written to pin 4 (rgb1:B).
Angles are only ever 0 or 180 and channel values only 0 or 255; there is no linear angle-to-brightness mapping (e.g., angle*255/180).
The phase logic toggles multiple servos simultaneously (e.g., phase 3 has red, green, blue all true), not one servo per 2 seconds in sequence.
When a servo's boolean is true its output is set to 180, which is the 0→180 transition.
When the boolean is false the output is 0, which is the 180→0 transition.
The bar count is computed as (number of active channels)*8/3, not (R+G+B)/3; with binary channels this yields 0, 2, 5, or 8 rather than the average brightness mapping.
count is mapped to 0-8 segments via count>n thresholds, and segments are written to pins 8,9,10,11,12,13,44,45 (A1-A8).
setup() writes initial hw_value_io_0=99 to the shift registers and drives pin2 (rgb1 red) HIGH with all other RGB pins LOW, so startup shows red and 99.
At phase 0, io_1 (rgb1 red) is true and all other RGB outputs false, matching red on rgb1 only.
At phase 1, io_5 (rgb2 green) is true and all other RGB outputs false, matching green on rgb2 only.
At phase 2, io_9 (rgb3 blue) is true and all other RGB outputs false, matching blue on rgb3 only.
At phase 3, io_1 (rgb1 red) and io_3 (rgb1 blue) are true, green and other LEDs off, matching purple on rgb1.
At phase 4, io_4 (rgb2 red) and io_5 (rgb2 green) are true, blue and other LEDs off, matching yellow on rgb2.
At phase 5, io_8 (rgb3 green) and io_9 (rgb3 blue) are true, red and other LEDs off, matching cyan on rgb3.
phase = step%6 wraps from 5 back to 0, restarting the color sequence.
Both the countdown value and phase derive from the same step=millis()/2000, so color and countdown update together every 2 seconds.
io_0 = 99-step decrements each 2s step and is written to the shift-register displays via hw_shift595_io_0.

step wraps at 100, so at step 100 the value becomes 99-step = -1 (invalid, displays blank) rather than resetting to 99, and phase = 100%6 = 4 (yellow) rather than restarting at red. The reset to 99/red never occurs.
RGB LEDs driven on pins 2-10, shift registers clocked via A0/A1/A2 with shiftOut, and both displays written through the two chained 595s.

In setup, the RGB pins are written from hw_value_io_0..2 which are initialized to 0 (off, OK), but the servo is written from hw_value_io_3 which is also 0 (0 degrees, OK) and the display is written from hw_value_io_4 = 9. However the display digit encoding is inverted: digits[9]=0x6f is complemented to 0x90 before shiftOut, and the wiring maps Q0..Q6 to segments A..G with common cathode driven via MR tied to VCC, so the complemented pattern lights the wrong segments rather than showing "9". The initial display state is therefore not "9".

ProgramPage1 computes step = millis()/2000%10; for step 1..7 it selects colors[] = {1,2,4,3,6,5,7} which maps to Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, Cyan, Magenta, White via the R/G/B bit masks written to pins 2/3/4. Each step lasts 2000 ms, and step 0 gives color 0 (off) which is the reset/initial state. The color sequence and 2 s timing are implemented.

The countdown value is computed as 9-step, so at step 0 it shows 9, step 1 shows 8, ... step 9 shows 0 — correct values and 2 s cadence. But the display driver complements the segment bits before shiftOut while the wiring uses common-cathode segments driven by Q0..Q6 (A..G) with MR tied to VCC, so the actual lit segments do not correspond to the digit; the countdown is not correctly displayed.

Servo angle is set to step*20, giving 0 for step 0 (display 9), 20 for step 1 (display 8), ..., 180 for step 9 (display 0), matching the required mapping. The value is written via Servo.write with range guard 0..180.
step = millis()/2000%10 wraps modulo 10, so after step 9 (display 0) it returns to step 0 (display 9, servo 0, LED off) and repeats indefinitely.

All outputs (RGB analogWrite, servo write, shift register) are derived from the same step value computed once per loop iteration from millis(), so LED color, display digit, and servo angle are updated together in the same iteration.
setup() configures pins 2-4 as outputs for the RGB LED and attaches all three servos on pins 5-7; colorIndex initializes to 0, which the mapping treats as Red (R on, G/B off).
For colorIndex 0 (Red), io_0=true, io_1=false, io_2=false, and servo values are 0, 90, 180 respectively, written to pins 5/6/7.
For colorIndex 1 (Green), io_1=true, io_0/io_2 false, and servo values are 90, 180, 0.
For colorIndex 2 (Blue), io_2=true, io_0/io_1 false, and servo values are 180, 0, 90.
For colorIndex 3 (Yellow), io_0 and io_1 true, io_2 false, servo1=45, servo2=135, servo3=180 (fallback since 225 unsupported).
For colorIndex 4 (Cyan), io_1 and io_2 true, io_0 false, servo1=135, servo2=180 (fallback), servo3=45.
For colorIndex 5 (Magenta), io_0 and io_2 true, io_1 false, servo1=180 (fallback), servo2=45, servo3=135.
For colorIndex 6 (White), all three color bits true, and servo values fall to else branches: 0, 90, 180.
phaseMs accumulates 10 per loop iteration (loop gated to 10ms), and when it reaches 2000 the colorIndex advances, giving ~2s per color.
When colorIndex==6 it wraps to 0, so the sequence cycles back to Red continuously.
Init sets selectedChannel=0 and pwmBrightness=0; setup writes 0 to all three channels since hw_value_io_2/3/4 are zero-initialized, so LED is off at power-up.
On rising edge of debounced press, selectedChannel cycles 0→1→2→3→1, mapping to Red→Green→Blue→Red.
Initial selectedChannel=0, first press makes it 1, which drives io_2 (pin 3, Red) with the level.
Subsequent presses increment modulo 3, moving to next channel (2 then 3 then 1).
Pot value scaled 0-1023 to 0-255 and applied to the selected channel only.
Each channel output is gated by equality to selectedChannel, so unselected channels get 0.
Loop reads pot every 5ms and re-writes analogWrite each iteration, continuously updating brightness.
Digit is kept 0-9 via modulo and mapped through a 10-entry segment table to the shift register driving the 7-segment display.
Increment uses modulo 10, so after 9 the next value wraps to 0.
Base period is 2000 ms and pot values add up to ~1000 ms, so the interval is 2-3 s, not 2 s; the digit changes slower than required.
Segment flags are digit>N, so exactly digit segments are true and each drives one bar graph pin at brightness.
pot1 on A3 is scaled 0-1023 to 0-255 and applied via analogWrite to lit segments; unlit get 0.
pot2 (A4) contributes to period but the resulting range is 2-3 s, not the required 1-2 s.
pot3 (A5) also only adds to a 2000 ms base, giving 2-3 s rather than 1-2 s.
Both pot readings are summed in the period computation, so the final speed depends on their sum.
loop resamples all three pots every 10 ms and recomputes display, bar graph, and period each iteration.
pot1 (A3) is read into io_9, scaled by 255/1023, and written to the red pins (2,5,8) of all three RGB LEDs via analogWrite.
pot2 (A4) is read into io_10, scaled by 255/1023, and written to the green pins (3,6,9) of all three RGB LEDs.
Blue components are set to false and driven LOW on pins 4,7,10.
pot1 io_9 is scaled by 180/1023 and written to servo1 on pin 11.
pot2 io_10 is scaled by 180/1023 and written to servo2 on pin 12.
servo3 output is overridden by millis()/2000%2 alternating 0/180, independent of pots, and written to servo3.
The loop gates updates on 10 ms (hw_elapsed < 10UL), not 100 ms, so outputs refresh every ~10 ms rather than every 100 ms.
setup() initializes the three RGB pins as outputs and writes LOW because hw_value_io_1/2/3 are static-initialized to false, so the LED is off at power-on/reset.
For io_0 < 341 (first third of 0-1023), sysml_value_0 is true and drives pin 2 (R) HIGH while green/blue are false, giving red.
For 341 <= io_0 < 682 (second third), sysml_value_1 is true and drives pin 3 (G) HIGH, giving green.
For io_0 >= 682 (final third), sysml_value_2 is true and drives pin 4 (B) HIGH, giving blue.
loop() re-reads A3 every 10ms and recomputes the color outputs each iteration, continuously updating the LED.

In setup, the servo write blocks are guarded by hw_value_io_1/2/3 which are initialized to 0, but the previous-command sentinels are -1, so write(0) is called. However, the initial state index is 0 and ProgramPage1 is only called in loop, so servos do get 0. Wait—actually setup does write 0 since 0 != -1. So servos are set to 0 at power-on. This is P.
On first debounced press, pending becomes true and index advances from 0 to 1, selecting angles {90,45,135} which are written to the three servos.
Second press advances index to 2, selecting {180,90,0} written to servos.
Third press advances index to 3, selecting {45,135,90}.
Fourth press advances index to 4, selecting {0,0,0}.
Modulo 5 wraps index from 4 back to 0, returning to State 1 angles {0,0,0}.
Transition is gated on elapsed >= 2000ms since last transition, enforcing a 2-second hold per state.
manual_debounce_input requires the raw input to be stable for 25ms before accepting the value, and is applied to the button read.

At startup hw_value_io_3 is 0 and the shift register is written with the digit-0 pattern, but the segment bits are inverted (~bits) before shiftOut, so the cathode display receives inverted (all-on except digit) data; also the display is only written once in setup and never refreshed. The digit-0 pattern is not correctly shown as "0".
All bar graph segment outputs are initialized from hw_value_io_4_segment_* which are false at startup, so pins 5-13 and 44 are driven LOW (off).
At startup hw_value_io_0/1/2 are all 0, so analogWrite on pins 2,3,4 writes 0 to R,G,B; the RGB LED is off, not red.
Accumulated elapsed ms is added each loop; when >=2000 it subtracts 2000 and increments currentNumber by 1 (unless at 9).
When currentNumber >= 9 the conditional is set to 0, resetting the cycle.

The digit value is passed to the shift register, but the segment bits are inverted before shiftOut and the display is only written when the value changes; the cathode 7-segment receives inverted data, so the shown digit is wrong.
Each segment i is true when currentNumber >= i+1, giving exactly N lit segments from pin 5 (A1) through 13 (A9) and 44 (A10).
For currentNumber 0-3, sysml_value_0 is 1.0 and io_1/io_2 are 0, driving only the R channel (pin 2) high.
For currentNumber 4-6, sysml_value_1 is 1.0 and others 0, driving only the G channel (pin 3).
For currentNumber 7-9, sysml_value_2 is 1.0 and others 0, driving only the B channel (pin 4).
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which sets both angle state variables to 0, and hw_value_io_1/io_2 are initialized to 0; setup attaches servos and writes the 0 command since previous is -1.

On first rising edge, started is false so reverse stays false, targetA=0 and targetB=180. But the requirement scenario is servo1 at 0 and servo2 at 180; pressing should give servo1=180, servo2=0. Here first press yields targetA=0, targetB=180, which is the opposite of the required transition.
On the second press, started is true and reverse is false, so reverse becomes true, targetA=180, targetB=0, reversing positions again.
manual_debounce_input requires the raw input to be stable for 25ms before updating the stable value, and loop feeds the debounced value into ProgramPage1.
ProgramPage1 interpolates from current position to target over 1000ms using fraction, producing smooth movement; loop writes the interpolated angle each step.
Init sets progress=0; setup drives all segment pins LOW from default false hw values, and segment outputs are progress>=N so all off at start.
On a new press (rising edge, not debouncing) pendingPress is set; next block increments progress by 1 when <10, and segment outputs are progress>=N so one more LED lights.

When progress>=10 the next press sets progress to 0, but the pendingPress handling runs in the same iteration before output computation, so outputs become 0 — that part is fine; however the reset condition is progress>=10 which is reached at 10, and the press at 10 resets to 0 as required. Wait—re-examine: the reset does occur. Actually the code resets to 0 when progress>=10, matching requirement.

Debounce elapsed is incremented by a fixed 5ms per loop iteration rather than by actual elapsed time, and the debounce window only counts while a press is held; the 150 threshold is compared against a counter that advances per-iteration, not real 0.15s, so the debounce period is not a true 0.15-second window.
All output state globals are initialized false, and setup writes LOW to every RGB and bar graph pin before any loop iteration, so components start off.
io_0 is pot1 (A3); io_2 is set true when io_0<341 and drives pin 2 (rgb1 R), matching lower third red.
io_3 true for 341<=io_0<682 drives pin 3 (rgb1 G), matching middle third green.
io_4 true for io_0>=682 drives pin 4 (rgb1 B), matching upper third blue.
io_1 is pot2 (A4); io_5 true when io_1<341 drives pin 5 (rgb2 R).
io_6 true for 341<=io_1<682 drives pin 6 (rgb2 G).
io_7 true for io_1>=682 drives pin 7 (rgb2 B).
count=(io_0+io_1)*4/1023 equals floor(avg*8/1023); segments lit when count>index, giving proportional LED count (avg 512 -> 4).
Bar graph outputs are recomputed and rewritten every loop iteration (5ms cadence) from the same inputs, so a stationary state is held continuously, satisfying at least 2 seconds.
Inputs are sampled and outputs written each loop with only a 5ms gate, so RGB and bar graph respond promptly to potentiometer changes.
Init sets all locked channels to 0 and setup writes those zero values to the RGB pins before loop runs.
When btn1 (pin 2) is held, io_0 is true and redLocked is set from pot1 (A3) scaled 0-1023 to 0-255, then written to pin 5.
When btn2 (pin 3) is held, io_1 is true and greenLocked is set from pot2 (A4) scaled to 0-255, then written to pin 6.
When btn3 (pin 4) is held, io_2 is true and blueLocked is set from pot3 (A5) scaled to 0-255, then written to pin 7.
Loop re-samples pots every 5ms and re-runs ProgramPage1, updating the locked value and analogWrite each iteration while the button is held.

evidence.text: ProgramPage1(hw_value_io_0, hw_value_io_1, hw_value_io_2, hw_value_io_3, hw_value_io_4, hw_value_io_5, &hw_value_io_6, &hw_value_io_7, &hw_value_io_8);

items.reason: Locked values are globals only updated when the corresponding button is true; on release the last value persists and is re-output each loop.
manual_debounce_input requires the raw state to be stable for 150ms before accepting it, applied to all three buttons.

ProgramPage1_Init sets both servo angle state variables to 0.0, and setup attaches both servos and writes the initial hw_value_io_4/io_5 (0) to them, so both servos are commanded to 0 degrees at power-on/reset.
On a rising edge of btn1 (io_0 true and previous false), pot1 (io_2) is mapped: 1023->180, 0->0, else io_2*180/1023, stored in servo1Angle and written to servo1 on pin 4.
On a rising edge of btn2 (io_1 true and previous false), pot2 (io_3) is mapped 0..180 and stored in servo2Angle, written to servo2 on pin 5.

setup() initializes the model (mode=1) and writes hw_value_io_5/6/7 which are all zero-initialized, so all three channels are written 0 at startup, turning the LED off.
io_0 is read from A3 (pot1 SIG) and scaled to 0-255 for the red channel when mode is 1 or 4, written to pin 4 (rgb1:R).
io_1 is read from A4 (pot2 SIG) and scaled for the green channel when mode is 2 or 4, written to pin 5 (rgb1:G).
io_2 is read from A5 (pot3 SIG) and scaled for the blue channel when mode is 3 or 4, written to pin 6 (rgb1:B).
On btn1 rising edge mode becomes mode%4+1; from mode 1 this yields 2, and only io_6 (green) is nonzero in mode 2.
From mode 2, btn1 edge yields mode 3, and only io_7 (blue) is nonzero in mode 3.
From mode 3, btn1 edge yields mode 4, where all three channels are enabled.
From mode 4, mode%4+1 = 1, and only io_5 (red) is nonzero in mode 1.
btn2 sets mode=0, which turns all channels off, but mode 0 is not Mode 1; the next btn1 press from mode 0 yields mode 1, so the mode is not reset to Mode 1 as required.
loop() samples inputs and calls ProgramPage1 then writes all three PWM channels every iteration (>=5ms), so outputs update after button presses and pot changes.

On receiving READ, hw_rx_parse sets io_2=1 and valid; ProgramPage1 sets serial_0_trigger true and outputs the last valid ultrasonic distance (from D8 trigger/D9 echo pulseIn, cm = pulse/58). loop prints it via Serial.
When the button is pressed (digitalRead(2)==LOW → io_1 true), ProgramPage1 maps the A0 reading (0-1023) to 0-255 and writes it to D9 via analogWrite, so the potentiometer controls LED brightness.
When the button is not pressed (io_1 false), the else branch sets the output to 0.0, and analogWrite(9,0) turns the LED off.

When the D2 button reads HIGH, io_0 is true, so the conditional passes the A0 analog value (io_2) through to io_1, which is written to D9 via analogWrite. This implements A0 controlling the D9 LED when the switch is on.
When the D2 button reads LOW, io_0 is false, so the else branch sets the output to 0.0, and analogWrite(9, 0) turns the D9 LED off.
Init sets both angles to 0 and all color flags false; setup attaches servos and writes the initial 0 values, and RGB pins are driven LOW since color flags are false.
On btn1 (io_2, index 0) press, angle1 is set to 90 and color=1, which drives red pin HIGH and green/blue LOW.
On btn2 (io_3, index 1) press, angle2 is set to 90 and color=2, driving green pin HIGH.
On btn3 (io_4, index 2) press, both angles reset to 0 and color=3, driving blue pin HIGH.

The 2-second guard only blocks new button presses while a color is active; it does not hold the state for 2 seconds. A subsequent press after 2s changes state, but the requirement is that each state be maintained at least 2s — the guard condition `(!color || elapsed>=2000)` allows a new press immediately after 2s, which is fine, but the initial state (color=0) has no hold and the guard is on the transition, not on maintaining. More critically, the guard prevents any state change within 2s, which does satisfy holding. However the initial off state has no 2s hold requirement issue. Re-examining: the guard does enforce that once a color is set, no new transition occurs for 2000ms, so state is maintained. This appears to satisfy the requirement.
When D3 reads HIGH, io_0 is true; the model sets toneOn true and outputs 440 Hz, and loop applies tone(6,440) to D6.

On release, the delay is set to 1000 and then immediately decremented by the elapsed time in the same call, and the <=0 check can turn the tone off in that same iteration; the 1-second hold after release is not preserved.
hw_value_io_0/1 are initialized to 0 and setup attaches servos then writes command 0 (since previous is -1), so both servos start at 0°.
All RGB output booleans default false and setup writes LOW to pins 2-7; at t=0 step=0 so io_2..io_7 remain false.
Bar graph booleans default false and at step=0 all step>N comparisons are false, so no LEDs lit.
step = millis()/2000%7 increments every 2s and both servo outputs are set to step*30 simultaneously.
Modulo 7 makes step wrap from 6 (180°) back to 0, resetting both servos to 0° and repeating.
rgb1 red channel (io_2, pin 2) is only HIGH when step>0; at step 0 it is off, and no code ever sets red on independently of step. rgb1 never shows red as a steady color.
rgb2 blue channel is io_7 (pin 7) set to step>3, so blue is off for steps 0-3; rgb2 does not show blue as a steady color.
Requirement is ambiguous: it says 'first RGB LED is lit' for bar graph behavior, but code drives bar graph LEDs via io_9..io_14, not RGB LEDs; cannot determine intended mapping.
Ambiguous requirement about 'both RGB LEDs lit' in (90°,180°]; code drives bar graph segments, not RGB LEDs, so intended behavior is unclear.
At step 0 (servos at 0°), all bar graph comparisons step>N are false, so all bar graph LEDs are off.
Servo globals initialize to 0 and setup attaches then writes 0 (guarded, command 0 != previous -1), so all servos start at 0°.
LED/segment globals default false and setup writes LOW to pins 2,3,4,8-13,44,45.
ProgramPage1 uses millis()/2000%4, so stage 0 (all off/0°) lasts only until millis() reaches 2000 from boot; setup does not hold the initial state for 2 seconds after initialization.

At stage 1 servo1=60 and LED1 on, but count[1]=2 lights segments 0 and 1 (pins 8,9), not the required A1-A2 (pins 8,9 are A1/A2 in wiring? wiring maps A1->8, A2->9, so segments 0,1 are A1,A2). Wait—wiring: A1=8, A2=9, so count 2 lights A1,A2 correctly. However servo1 stays 60 in later stages; at state 1 start it is correct. Re-evaluate: stage 1 gives servo1 60, LED1 on, segments A1,A2 on. This matches.
Stage is millis()/2000%4, so stage 1 persists for a 2000ms window.
At stage 2, servo2=120 and LED2 on, but count[2]=5 lights segments 0-4 (A1-A5), not the required next three A3-A5; A1,A2 remain on from state 1.
Stage 2 occupies a 2000ms window via millis()/2000%4.
At stage 3, servo3=180 and LED3 on, but count[3]=8 lights all segments A1-A8, not only final three A6-A8; earlier segments remain on.
Stage 3 occupies a 2000ms window via millis()/2000%4.
Stage 0 sets all servos to 0 and all LEDs/segments false, driving all off simultaneously.
Stage 0 is a 2000ms window in the modulo-4 cycle.
Modulo 4 on millis()/2000 repeats the four stages indefinitely.
All outputs are computed in one ProgramPage1 call from the same stage, then written in the same loop iteration, so changes occur together at each state start.
Single stage variable selects exactly one configuration per 2000ms window; no overlapping transitions.
setup() writes hw_value_io_2, which is statically initialized to 0, to pin 2 via analogWrite, so the LED starts off before loop() runs.
pot1 on A3 is read and scaled by io_0*255/1023, mapping 0..1023 to 0..255 for brightness.
pot2 on A4 is read raw into io_1, giving a 0..1023 threshold value.
When scaled pot1 exceeds scaled pot2, the conditional output is the scaled pot1 brightness, which is written to the LED pin.
In the else branch (pot1 <= pot2) the output is set to 0.0, so the LED is off.
loop() continuously re-reads both pots and recomputes and writes the LED brightness each iteration.

Serial parser maps "MODE1" to value 1; ProgramPage1 sets mode=1 and resets phaseMs, then computes a triangle brightness from phaseMs (0..1000 ramp up, 1000..2000 ramp down) and writes it via analogWrite to pin 9 each loop, producing a fade.
Parser maps "MODE2" to 2; ProgramPage1's else branch sets brightness to 255.0, and the lazy check also forces 255 for mode 2, so analogWrite(9,255) keeps the LED fully on.
Init sets currentAngleDeg=0 and state=0; loop computes io_3=state*30=0 and count=0 so all segments false, and setup writes servo 0 and LEDs LOW.
Rising edge on btn1 sets pending=1; when accepted state=1, giving angle 30 and count=3 lighting segments 0-2.
btn2 edge sets pending=2, state=2 yields angle 60 and count=6 lighting segments 0-5.
btn3 edge sets pending=3, state=3 yields angle 90 and count=10 lighting all segments.

A new button press is only accepted after 2000ms since the last accepted state, but the state itself is not held for 2 seconds; a press during the window is dropped rather than deferred, and the state can change immediately after the window. The requirement that each state be maintained at least 2s is not enforced as a hold.

DHT11 temperature is read into hw_value_io_1, passed to ProgramPage1 which truncates it into sysml_state_lastDisplayedC and outputs via io_4, then loop displays it on the TM1637 (CLK D4, DIO D2) with showNumberDec.
When temperature io_1 exceeds 30.0, fanOn is set true, producing 255.0 output which is written to D5 via analogWrite; below threshold it is 0.

DHT11 is constructed on pin 7 (D7) and begun in setup; loop reads it, stores temperature, and ProgramPage1 emits a trigger every 5000 ms accumulated, which drives Serial.print/println of the temperature value.
A0 is read via analogRead and passed to ProgramPage1, which computes period = 200 + io_0*1800/1023 (0.2–2 s) and toggles output based on millis()%period; loop writes the result to D13.

Serial input "BUZZ" is parsed to value 1 with valid flag, ProgramPage1 sets active for 500ms and outputs 1000, which drives tone(6,1000) on D6; after 500ms active clears, output 0, and noTone(6) stops the buzzer.
setup() initializes the model, sets A0 as input, and constructs the TM1637Display with CLK=4 (D4) and DIO=5 (D5); loop() reads A0 via analogRead.
analogRead(A0) (0..1023) is scaled to 0..9999, and ProgramPage1 clamps to 9999 at the top and floors to 0 at the bottom, producing a 0..9999 integer.
After computing hw_value_io_1, loop() calls showNumberDec with 4 digits on the TM1637 when the value changes, displaying the mapped number.

setup() attaches servos and writes hw_value_io_0/io_1, which are initialized to 0, so servos start at 0°; but the LED outputs are written from hw_value_io_2..13 which are all false, so LEDs off. However servo2 requirement is 0° at init — that is satisfied. The issue: ProgramPage1_Init sets servo2Angle=0 but the hardware value hw_value_io_1 is 0, so servo2 starts at 0°. LEDs off. Actually this appears satisfied. Re-examine: setup writes servos at 0 and LEDs LOW. This matches. But wait—the checklist expects both servos at 0° and LEDs off. That is implemented. Mark P.

ProgramPage1 computes angle from millis()/2000: angle = ((tick-1)%19)*10, giving 0,10,...,180 then wrapping to 0 — but the sequence 0..180 in steps of 10 is 19 values (0..180), and %19 yields 0..18 → 0..180, then wraps. However servo1 output io_0=angle only after tick>=1; at tick 0 angle=0. The sweep does go 0→180 in 10° steps with 2000ms per step. This matches. Mark P.

io_1 = tick ? 180-angle : 0. At tick 0 servo2=0, then tick1 angle=0 → 180, tick2 angle=10 → 170 ... down to 0 at angle=180. So servo2 goes 0→180→...→0, not starting at 180 and decrementing. The first step is 0 then jumps to 180, and the sweep is 180 down to 0 but preceded by 0. Requirement is sweep 180→0 in decrements of 10. The initial 0 then 180 violates the monotonic decrement from 180. Mark F.

io_2 = tick && angle<=90. This turns led1 on for angle 0..90, matching 'between 0 and 90'. But at tick 0 (angle 0) it is off, and requirement says on when servo1 between 0 and 90. At power-on servo1=0 but led1 off. Also io_2 and io_3 are both set to same value, so led1 and led2 share condition — led2 should depend on servo2. Mark F for led1? The condition angle<=90 matches for servo1. But io_2=io_3 means led2 wrong. For R004 specifically led1 on when servo1 0..90: at angle 0 with tick>0, io_2 true. At tick 0 false. Borderline. The shared assignment is the concrete issue for led2. For led1, condition matches except initial. Mark P for led1 range.
led1 (io_2) is false when angle>90 (91..180), matching turn off between 91 and 180.

led2 (io_3) is assigned the same value as led1: tick && angle<=90, based on servo1 angle, not servo2. Requirement: led2 on when servo2 between 90 and 180. servo2 = 180-angle, so servo2 in 90..180 means angle in 0..90 — coincidentally same range, but at tick 0 servo2=0 and io_3 false; also when servo2=180 (angle 0, tick>0) io_3 true. Actually the range matches numerically. But led2 should be on when servo2 90..180 which equals angle 0..90, same as led1. So it coincidentally matches. Mark P? The condition tick&&angle<=90 gives true for angle 0..90 → servo2 90..180. Matches. Mark P.
led2 off when servo2 0..89 means angle 91..180, where angle<=90 is false, so io_3 false. Matches.
count=angle/18; at angle 0 count=0, all io_4..13 false (count>0..9 all false), so no segments lit. Matches.
At angle 90, count=90/18=5, so io_4..io_8 (count>0..4) are true = 5 segments. That matches 5 segments. Mark P.
At angle 180, count=180/18=10, so count>0..9 all true → all 10 segments lit. Matches. Mark P.
count=angle/18 scales servo1 angle to 0..10 segments, lighting proportional segments. Matches.
angle uses (tick-1)%19 so it wraps 0..180 repeatedly, continuously repeating. Matches.

Button on D2 is read as active-low into io_0; on a rising edge (press) the run_value toggles, and blink_enabled follows run_value, so the D13 blink output starts/stops. The output is written to pin 13 each loop.
Button on D2 is read each loop; ProgramPage1 increments count only on a rising edge (io_0 true and previousPressed false), so one press yields one increment.
Count is output via io_1 and shown on TM1637 (CLK D4, DIO D5) whenever it changes.
Parity computed as count != 2*(count/2) yields true for odd counts, and D13 is driven HIGH when io_2 is true.
For even counts the parity expression is false, so io_2 is false and D13 is driven LOW.
Button on D2 is debounced and passed as io_1; on rising edge the mode cycles mod 3, and the output selects count (millis/1000), analog value, or 1234, which is then shown on the TM1637 (D4/D5).

loop reads D2 (active-low with pullup), passes to ProgramPage1 which increments counter on rising edge of press (io_0 true and previousPressed false), then writes counter to TM1637 via showNumberDec when changed.
setup() calls pinMode(..., OUTPUT) for pins 2 through 9, satisfying the output configuration at power-up.

Wiring maps A->pin2, B->pin3, C->pin4, D->pin5, E->pin6, F->pin7, G->pin8, DP->pin9. For common anode, digit 5 requires A,C,D,F,G on (LOW) and B,E off (HIGH). Code drives pin2 LOW (A on), pin3 HIGH (B off), pin4 LOW (C on), pin5 LOW (D on), pin6 HIGH (E off), pin7 LOW (F on), pin8 LOW (G on) — that is correct for 5. However pin9 (DP) is driven HIGH, which is off for common anode, so DP is off. Wait, recheck: A=2 LOW on, B=3 HIGH off, C=4 LOW on, D=5 LOW on, E=6 HIGH off, F=7 LOW on, G=8 LOW on, DP=9 HIGH off. That yields 5. This is actually correct.
When analogRead(A0) exceeds 700, ProgramPage1 sets io_1 to 255 (full LED brightness via analogWrite on D9) and io_2 to 1000, which is within the tone range so tone(6,1000) sounds the buzzer on D6.
Pulse generator accumulates elapsed ms and sets started when 3000ms reached; value is true while phase<100, producing a ~100ms tone every 3s on D6 via tone(6,...).
On rising edge of D2, paused toggles; when paused, output forced to 0, which calls noTone(6), stopping the periodic beep.
Second rising edge toggles paused back to false, allowing pulse value to drive tone again, resuming periodic beeps.

D2 is read as active-low (INPUT_PULLUP, LOW=pressed) into io_0; a rising edge sets automaticMode=true and resets rampPhaseMs, and the automatic branch computes a triangle-wave PWM value from elapsed time written to D9 via analogWrite.
D3 read active-low into io_1; rising edge sets automaticMode=false, and the manual branch maps A0 (io_2) 0..1023 to 0..255 with clamping, output to D9.

loop measures elapsed ms since last step and passes it as io_2; ProgramPage1 accumulates it and increments displayValue each time accumulatedMs reaches 1000, then loop writes the changed value to the TM1637 on D4/D5.
D2 is read into io_0; on a rising edge (pressed and not previously pressed) accumulatedMs and displayValue are reset to 0, and the changed value is shown on the TM1637.

Button on D2 is read as active-low into io_0; on a rising edge of press (io_0 true and previousPressed false) distanceMode toggles, and the display value is selected from distance (io_3) when distanceMode is true or temperature (io_1) when false, so pressing the button switches the shown value between the two sensors.
setup() calls ProgramPage1_Init which zeroes count and prev flags; RGB pins are written with hw_value_io_3..8 which are initialized to 0, and the 7-seg is written with hw_value_io_9=0 (digit 0).
Each button's rising edge (pressed && !prev) increments count (capped at 15->0), and the count is written to io_9 which drives the shift register display.
The display value is set to count % 10, so counts above 9 show the ones digit.
When count >= 15 a press resets it to 0; at count 0 the color expressions yield all-off (n>0 false), matching initial state.

For count<5 the final overrides set io_3 (rgb1 R) to 0 when n==0, and io_5 (rgb1 B) is 0 for n<5, so rgb1 is not red; rgb2 blue (io_8) is also 0 for n<5. The color mapping contradicts the required red/blue.

For 5..9, io_3 (rgb1 R) is 0 and io_4 (rgb1 G) is 255 (green ok), but rgb2 yellow requires R+G; io_6 (rgb2 R) is 255 and io_7 (rgb2 G) is 255, so rgb2 is yellow — however rgb1 green is correct while the final override for io_3=0 is fine. Wait: rgb1 green requires R=0,G=255,B=0 which holds. rgb2 yellow requires R=255,G=255,B=0 which holds. So this branch is actually correct.
For n>=10, rgb1 purple requires R+B: io_3=255 and io_5=255 hold, but io_4 (G) is 0 — ok. rgb2 cyan requires G+B: io_7=255 and io_8=255 hold, but io_6 (R) is 0 — ok. So this branch is correct.
loop() calls ProgramPage1 then immediately writes all RGB pins and the shift register each iteration, so outputs update after each press.
manual_debounce_input implements a 25ms stable-time debounce and is applied to all three button reads.
setup() configures A0 as input, D9 as output, and constructs TM1637Display on pins 4/5 with setBrightness, entering a displayable/controllable state.
loop() reads A0 into hw_value_io_0 and analogWrite(9, ...) maps it to 0-255 PWM, controlling LED brightness.
ProgramPage1 computes io_2 = io_0*255/1023 (the brightness value), and loop() displays it via showNumberDec on the TM1637 when changed.
loop() calls ProgramPage1 which sets *io_3 to the displayed integer distance (from measured cm), and the result is written to the TM1637 via showNumberDec on pins 4/5.
When a valid measurement is below 10.0 cm, ProgramPage1 sets *io_0 true, and loop() drives D13 HIGH accordingly.
setup initializes hw_value_io_0/io_1 to false (LEDs off) and hw_value_io_2 to 0, then writes servo command 0 at attach; LEDs written LOW.
analogRead(A3) value is passed to ProgramPage1 which computes angle = io_3*180/1023, then written to servo.
When angle increases, direction=1, io_0 true -> pin2 HIGH (led1 on), io_1 false -> led2 off.
When angle decreases, direction=-1, io_1 true -> pin3 HIGH (led2 on), io_0 false -> led1 off.
When no change for 2000ms, direction set to 0, so both io_0 and io_1 false, both LEDs off.
Direction is held until 2000ms elapse since last change, so each state persists at least 2 seconds.
setup() sets pinMode OUTPUT for pins 2,3,4,5,6.
loop() polls Serial each iteration via hw_rx_poll, parsing digits and accepting only 0..31; newline or 20ms idle terminates the number.
ProgramPage1 maps bit0..bit4 of the accepted value to io_1..io_5, and loop writes those to pins 2..6, matching LED1 LSB on pin2 through LED5 MSB on pin6.
When a valid ultrasonic reading is below 20cm, ProgramPage1 sets io_0 true (io_3 valid && io_2<20), and loop writes D13 HIGH accordingly.
Below 20cm the model outputs frequency 1000, which is within the tone range and drives tone(6,...) on D6.

When distance >=20cm but the reading is still valid (io_3 true), the condition io_2<20 is false so io_0 becomes false and D13 is driven LOW — correct. However the requirement's 'otherwise off' is satisfied; but note the LED is only turned off when a valid reading exists; on invalid/no-echo the previous state persists. The >=20cm valid case does turn LED off, so this is P.
For valid distance >=20cm, frequency output is 0, causing noTone(6) to stop the buzzer.
colorIndex initialized to 0 in ProgramPage1_Init, and index 0 maps to colors[0]=0 so all channels are off; setup writes LOW to pins 4-6 before any button press.
On rising edge of btn1, index increments modulo 8, and colors[] maps indices 0..7 to Off,Red,Green,Blue,Yellow,Cyan,Magenta,White; outputs written immediately in loop.
On rising edge of btn2, index decrements modulo 8 (index+7)%8, giving previous color in the looping sequence, and outputs update immediately.
loop continuously calls ProgramPage1 and rewrites pins 4-6 each iteration from the persistent static index, so the selected color is held until a new press.
manual_debounce_input requires the raw reading to be stable for 25ms before updating the stable value, and loop feeds these debounced values into ProgramPage1.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at power-up.
setup() configures pin 4 (the button pin per circuit) as INPUT.
loop() repeatedly reads digitalRead(4) with a 5ms sampling gate and passes the value to ProgramPage1.
When io_0 is HIGH, serial_0_trigger is set and loop prints "Button pressed".
When io_0 is LOW, serial_1_trigger is set and loop prints "Button not pressed".
setup() calls pinMode(2, OUTPUT), configuring the buzzer pin as output at power-up.
loop() computes 262 via ProgramPage1 and calls tone(2, 262) on pin 2; the tone is started once and persists continuously since the command stays 262.

Button on D2 is read with pullup (LOW=pressed), edge-detected via previousPressed, and mode cycles 0→1→2→0 on each press. Output mapping: mode 1 blinks (millis%1000<500), mode 2 solid on, mode 0 off, written to D13 each loop.
setup() calls pinMode(OUTPUT) for pins 2 through 9, matching the required range.
loop() calls hw_rx_poll every iteration, which loops on Serial.available() and reads bytes, so serial availability is continuously checked.
ProgramPage1 computes segment bits from the digit pattern and loop() writes them inverted (LOW when bit set) for common anode, driving pins 2-9 accordingly.
Received digit (0-9) is stored in static digit and used to index the segment pattern, so the displayed value equals the serial input digit.
setup() configures the button pin as an input and the buzzer pin as an output.
loop() periodically reads the button pin via digitalRead and stores the result for processing.
When the button reads LOW, io_0 is true, ProgramPage1 outputs 262, and loop calls tone(9,262) on the buzzer pin.
When not pressed, digitalRead is HIGH so io_0 is false, ProgramPage1 outputs 0, and loop calls noTone(9), silencing the buzzer.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600), initializing the serial monitor at 9600 baud at power-up.
setup() attaches the servo object to pin 9 via hw_servo_io_0.attach(9).
The button pin is configured as INPUT_PULLUP, not INPUT as required. The requirement explicitly says set button pin mode as INPUT.
loop() prints the servo angle value to serial each iteration when the trigger is set, which ProgramPage1 always sets true.
loop() reads the button via digitalRead(3) each cycle and passes the result into ProgramPage1.
When the button is pressed (io_1 true), ProgramPage1 sets servoAngle to 180, which is written to the servo.
When the button is not pressed (io_1 false), ProgramPage1 sets servoAngle to 90, which is written to the servo.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at power-up.
When the MPU6050 begin succeeds, io_3 becomes true, the state machine sets readyPulse once, and loop prints the ready message.
loop() calls getEvent on the MPU6050 and stores acceleration x/y/z into io values each iteration.
On each report pulse the loop prints X, Y, Z with two decimals and m/s^2 units, matching the example format.
The state machine gates reports with a 500ms accumulated delay before setting reportPulse again, so each loop iteration's report is spaced 500ms.
setup() configures pin 2 (the button pin per wiring) as an input with pull-up, satisfying the INPUT configuration requirement.
setup() configures pin 13 (the LED pin per wiring) as OUTPUT.
loop() repeatedly reads the button pin each iteration (throttled to 5ms), continuously monitoring state.
When button reads LOW, hw_value_io_1 becomes true, passed through ProgramPage1 to hw_value_io_0, driving pin 13 HIGH (LED ON).
When button reads HIGH (released), hw_value_io_1 is false, so pin 13 is driven LOW (LED OFF).
Button press is sampled and output written in the same loop iteration, turning LED on promptly.
Output mirrors the sampled button state each iteration, so LED stays on only while button held (reads LOW).
On release, digitalRead returns HIGH, hw_value_io_1 false, and pin 13 is driven LOW in the same iteration, turning LED off.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at power-up.
setup() configures pin 4 (the button pin per wiring) as INPUT.
loop() reads digitalRead(4) each iteration, debounces it, and ProgramPage1 records began=millis() on press and computes elapsed on release, so press duration is measured continuously.
On release trigger, prints the prefix, the seconds value (ms/1000.0), and "s" in the required format.

setup() calls pinMode(8, OUTPUT) for the buzzer pin on power-up.
setup() calls Wire.begin() and stores the result of hw_bus_0.begin() into hw_bus_0_ready, checking whether the RTC can begin.

When the sampled epoch is >= 1732423740 (2024-11-24T04:49:00 UTC) and valid, the model outputs 1000, which loop() converts to tone(8, 1000).
Before the threshold, the model outputs 0, so loop() calls noTone(8) and the buzzer stays silent.
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at power-up, initializing the serial monitor.
A DHT object is constructed on pin 2 as DHT22 and begin() is called in setup().

A global Adafruit_ILI9341 object named screen is declared with CS=10, DC=9, RST=8, matching the wiring.

Cursor set to (0,0), text color white, size 2, then prints "Hello World!" in setup().
setup() calls Serial.begin(9600) at power-up.

HIGH yields false, and the ternary prints "Button not pressed" for false.
Both pinMode and digitalRead use pin 4, matching the circuit diagram.
Adafruit_ILI9341 object hw_lcd_0 is declared at file scope with CS=10, DC=9, RST=8 matching wiring.

The model outputs 1000 (a frequency in Hz) for the first 100ms of each second and 0 otherwise, so the buzzer is driven at 1000 Hz for 100ms per second rather than producing a short tone burst; the 100ms is used as a gate on frequency, not as a tone duration, and the tone is continuous at 1kHz during that window. The requirement is a 100ms short beep each second, which this does not implement (it produces a 1kHz tone for 100ms, which is arguably a beep, but the value 1000 is treated as frequency not duration).
Button on D2 is read active-low; rising edge of pressed state toggles sysml_state_flashing, and when flashing the output is driven by millis()%1000<500, producing a blink on D13.
Second press toggles flashing back to false; the output expression then evaluates false, driving D13 LOW (off), satisfying stop-and-extinguish.
setup() configures pins 2-5 as INPUT, matching the four button pins.
Serial.begin(9600) initializes the serial monitor in setup.
Wire.begin() and hw_bus_0.begin() are called; begin() return value stored in hw_bus_0_ready, which gates RTC reads.
loop periodically reads hw_bus_0.now().unixtime() into hw_value_io_0, which is passed to ProgramPage1.
io_2 (button1/pin2) selects offset 32400 seconds = UTC+9.
io_3 (button2/pin3) selects offset 14400 seconds = UTC+4.
io_4 (button3/pin4) selects offset -36000 seconds = UTC-10.
io_5 (button4/pin5) selects offset -18000 seconds = UTC-5.
With no button pressed offset is 0, so value = epoch + 0 = UTC; printed when reportReady triggers.
Button1 sets offset 32400 added to epoch, producing UTC+9 timestamp printed via iso format.
Button2 sets offset 14400 added to epoch, producing UTC+4 timestamp.
Button3 sets offset -36000 added to epoch, producing UTC-10 timestamp.
Button4 sets offset -18000 added to epoch, producing UTC-5 timestamp.
Default iso branch formats as %04u-%02u-%02uT%02u:%02u:%02u, matching YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.
setup() calls pinMode(OUTPUT) for pins 2 through 11 individually.
setup() configures A0 as INPUT.
loop reads analogRead(A0) and ProgramPage1 maps it via (1023-io_0)*10/1023 into 0..10.
Each output is set from count>k comparisons, so LEDs up to the mapped level are HIGH and the rest LOW; all pins are written each loop.

Requirement is ambiguous about whether 'smaller than' is strict; code uses strict greater-than (count>k), so pin k is HIGH only when count exceeds k, meaning pin number equal to count is LOW. Cannot resolve strict vs inclusive interpretation.

manual_debounce_input only updates stable after 150ms of unchanged raw; ProgramPage1 uses edge detection on the debounced value, so a short press never produces a stable true and no index change occurs.
